     // video timestamp in seconds\n  description: string;    // Gemini-generated description of what's on screen\n  imagePath: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy A: VTT↔Otter text match.\n * Parse both VTT and Otter segments, fuzzy-match text segments (>60% word overlap),\n * calculate offset per match, return median.\n */\nexport function calculateWordOverlap(textA: string, textB: string): number {\n  const wordsA = new Set(textA.toLowerCase().split(/\\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 3));\n  const wordsB = new Set(textB.toLowerCase().split(/\\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 3));\n  if (wordsA.size === 0 || wordsB.size === 0) return 0;\n  const intersection = [...wordsA].filter(w => wordsB.has(w)).length;\n  const minSize = Math.min(wordsA.size, wordsB.size);\n  return intersection / minSize;\n}\n\nexport function strategyA(\n  vttSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n): OffsetResult | null {\n  const matches: number[] = [];\n\n  for (const vtt of vttSegments) {\n    for (const otter of otterSegments) {\n      const overlap = calculateWordOverlap(vtt.text, otter.text);\n      if (overlap >= 0.6) {\n        // offset = otterTime - videoTime\n        matches.push(otter.startTime - vtt.startTime);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (matches.length < 3) return null;\n\n  matches.sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const median = matches[Math.floor(matches.length / 2)];\n  const variance = matches.reduce((sum, m) => sum + Math.abs(m - median), 0) / matches.length;\n\n  return {\n    offsetSeconds: median,\n    confidence: variance < 5 ? 'high' : variance < 15 ? 'medium' : 'low',\n    strategy: 'vtt_text_match',\n    matchCount: matches.length,\n    varianceSeconds: variance,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy B: Gemini visual↔Otter keyword match.\n * Pick scene-change frames, get Gemini descriptions, search Otter for keywords,\n * calculate offset from matches.\n *\n * frameDescriptions: pre-classified frames with Gemini descriptions (from frame-classifier).\n * otterSegments: parsed Otter transcript.\n */\nexport function strategyB(\n  frameDescriptions: FrameDescription[],\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n): OffsetResult | null {\n  // Pick up to 5 well-spaced frames\n  const picked = pickSpacedFrames(frameDescriptions, 5);\n  if (picked.length === 0) return null;\n\n  const matches: number[] = [];\n\n  for (const frame of picked) {\n    // Extract keywords from Gemini description (nouns, app-specific terms)\n    const keywords = extractKeywords(frame.description);\n    if (keywords.length === 0) continue;\n\n    // Find best matching Otter segment\n    let bestScore = 0;\n    let bestOtterTime = 0;\n    for (const otter of otterSegments) {\n      const score = keywords.filter(kw =>\n        otter.text.toLowerCase().includes(kw.toLowerCase())\n      ).length / keywords.length;\n      if (score > bestScore) {\n        bestScore = score;\n        bestOtterTime = otter.startTime;\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (bestScore >= 0.3) {\n      matches.push(bestOtterTime - frame.timestamp);\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (matches.length < 2) return null;\n\n  matches.sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const median = matches[Math.floor(matches.length / 2)];\n  const variance = matches.reduce((sum, m) => sum + Math.abs(m - median), 0) / matches.length;\n\n  return {\n    offsetSeconds: median,\n    confidence: variance < 10 ? 'high' : variance < 30 ? 'medium' : 'low',\n    strategy: 'gemini_visual_match',\n    matchCount: matches.length,\n    varianceSeconds: variance,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy C: Manual entry fallback.\n */\nexport function strategyManual(offsetSeconds: number): OffsetResult {\n  return {\n    offsetSeconds,\n    confidence: 'high',\n    strategy: 'manual',\n    matchCount: 0,\n    varianceSeconds: 0,\n  };\n}\n\nexport function pickSpacedFrames(frames: FrameDescription[], count: number): FrameDescription[] {\n  if (frames.length <= count) return frames;\n  const step = frames.length / count;\n  const picked: FrameDescription[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n    picked.push(frames[Math.floor(i * step)]);\n  }\n  return picked;\n}\n\nexport function extractKeywords(description: string): string[] {\n  // Extract meaningful words (4+ chars, not common stop words)\n  const stopWords = new Set([\n    'this', 'that', 'with', 'from', 'have', 'been', 'were', 'they',\n    'will', 'would', 'could', 'should', 'there', 'their', 'about',\n    'which', 'when', 'what', 'some', 'other', 'than', 'then', 'also',\n    'just', 'more', 'very', 'into', 'over', 'such', 'after', 'before',\n    'between', 'each', 'being', 'does', 'doing', 'during', 'having',\n    'image', 'shows', 'showing', 'screen', 'appears', 'displayed',\n    'visible', 'window', 'application',\n  ]);\n  return description\n    .split(/[\\s,;:.!?()]+/)\n    .filter(w => w.length >= 4 && !stopWords.has(w.toLowerCase()))\n    .map(w => w.toLowerCase());\n}\n\n/**\n * Main entry point. Tries strategies in order: A → B → null (caller should prompt for manual).\n */\nexport async function calculateOffset(\n  vttSegments: TranscriptSegment[] | null,\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  frameDescriptions: FrameDescription[],\n): Promise<OffsetResult | null> {\n  // Strategy A: VTT↔Otter text match (fastest, most accurate when VTT available)\n  if (vttSegments && vttSegments.length > 0) {\n    const resultA = strategyA(vttSegments, otterSegments);\n    if (resultA && resultA.confidence !== 'low') {\n      return resultA;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Strategy B: Gemini visual↔Otter keyword match\n  if (frameDescriptions.length > 0 && otterSegments.length > 0) {\n    const resultB = strategyB(frameDescriptions, otterSegments);\n    if (resultB) {\n      return resultB;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // No automated strategy produced confident result\n  return null;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/offset-calculator.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **calculateWordOverlap** — 100% overlap returns 1.0, 0% returns 0, partial returns correct ratio, ignores short words (<4 chars)\n2. **strategyA** — returns high-confidence result when 5+ VTT/Otter segments match with >60% overlap, returns null with fewer than 3 matches, calculates correct median offset, variance reflects spread\n3. **strategyB** — returns result when keywords match Otter segments, returns null when no keywords match, picks spaced frames correctly\n4. **pickSpacedFrames** — returns all frames if count >= frames.length, picks evenly spaced frames otherwise\n5. **extractKeywords** — filters stop words, filters short words, lowercases\n6. **calculateOffset** — tries strategy A first when VTT available, falls back to B when A returns null, falls back to B when A returns low confidence, returns null when both fail, skips A when no VTT segments\n7. **strategyManual** — returns correct result with high confidence and manual strategy\n\nUse mock TranscriptSegment data — do NOT read real files in unit tests. Example segments:\n```typescript\nconst vttSegments: TranscriptSegment[] = [\n  { startTime: 100, endTime: 130, text: 'Looking at the contract management screen with vendor details' },\n  { startTime: 200, endTime: 230, text: 'Now showing the purchase order entry form fields' },\n  // ... more\n];\nconst otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[] = [\n  { startTime: 156, endTime: 186, text: 'Looking at the contract management screen with vendor details', speaker: 'Jason' },\n  { startTime: 256, endTime: 286, text: 'Now showing the purchase order entry form fields', speaker: 'Jason' },\n  // ... more — offset is 56 seconds\n];\n```\n\n---\n\n### File 2: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-classifier.ts`\n\n```typescript\nimport { google } from '@ai-sdk/google';\nimport { generateText } from 'ai';\nimport { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport { detectMediaType } from './analyze';\n\nexport interface ClassifiedFrame {\n  imagePath: string;\n  timestamp: number;       // video timestamp in seconds\n  isScreen: boolean;\n  description: string;     // Gemini description — reused for offset calculation\n  filterReason?: string;   // 'face' | 'transition' | 'blank' | 'other' if not a screen\n}\n\n/**\n * Classify a batch of frames using Gemini.\n * Batches 4-6 frames at a time to reduce API calls.\n * Returns classification + description for each frame.\n */\nexport async function classifyFrames(\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n  batchSize: number = 4,\n): Promise<ClassifiedFrame[]> {\n  const results: ClassifiedFrame[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < frames.length; i += batchSize) {\n    const batch = frames.slice(i, i + batchSize);\n    const batchResults = await classifyBatch(batch);\n    results.push(...batchResults);\n  }\n\n  return results;\n}\n\nexport async function classifyBatch(\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n): Promise<ClassifiedFrame[]> {\n  const fileParts = await Promise.all(\n    frames.map(async (frame) => {\n      const data = await readFile(frame.imagePath);\n      const mediaType = detectMediaType(frame.imagePath);\n      return { type: 'file' as const, data, mediaType };\n    }),\n  );\n\n  const prompt = `You are classifying ${frames.length} video frames. For EACH frame (numbered 1 to ${frames.length}), determine:\n\n1. Is this a software application screen? (Yes/No)\n2. Brief description of what's shown (10-20 words)\n3. If not a software screen, why? (face/transition/blank/other)\n\nA \"software application screen\" means a desktop or web application UI with forms, fields, menus, buttons, or data grids. Zoom meeting participant video, webcam feeds, desktop backgrounds, and loading screens are NOT software screens.\n\nReply in this exact format, one line per frame:\nFRAME 1: [YES|NO] | [description] | [reason if NO]\nFRAME 2: [YES|NO] | [description] | [reason if NO]\n...`;\n\n  const { text } = await generateText({\n    model: google('gemini-2.5-flash'),\n    messages: [\n      {\n        role: 'user',\n        content: [\n          ...fileParts,\n          { type: 'text', text: prompt },\n        ],\n      },\n    ],\n  });\n\n  return parseClassificationResponse(text, frames);\n}\n\nexport function parseClassificationResponse(\n  response: string,\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n): ClassifiedFrame[] {\n  const lines = response.split('\\n').filter(l => l.trim().startsWith('FRAME'));\n  const results: ClassifiedFrame[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < frames.length; i++) {\n    const line = lines[i];\n    if (!line) {\n      // Default to keeping unclassified frames as screens (conservative)\n      results.push({\n        imagePath: frames[i].imagePath,\n        timestamp: frames[i].timestamp,\n        isScreen: true,\n        description: 'Classification unavailable',\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    const parts = line.split('|').map(p => p.trim());\n    const isScreen = parts[0]?.toUpperCase().includes('YES') ?? false;\n    const description = parts[1] || 'No description';\n    const filterReason = !isScreen ? (parts[2] || 'other') : undefined;\n\n    results.push({\n      imagePath: frames[i].imagePath,\n      timestamp: frames[i].timestamp,\n      isScreen,\n      description,\n      filterReason,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return results;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-classifier.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **parseClassificationResponse** — parses YES responses correctly, parses NO responses with filter reason, handles missing lines (defaults to isScreen=true), handles empty response\n2. **classifyFrames** — batches correctly (10 frames with batchSize=4 → 3 batches), passes frames to classifyBatch\n3. Mock the Gemini call in classifyBatch — vi.mock `@ai-sdk/google` and `ai` as done in existing tests\n\n---\n\n### File 3: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-dedup.ts`\n\n```typescript\nimport sharp from 'sharp';\nimport type { ClassifiedFrame } from './frame-classifier';\n\nexport interface FrameGroup {\n  frames: ClassifiedFrame[];\n  representative: ClassifiedFrame;  // first frame in group\n}\n\nexport interface DedupResult {\n  selectedFrames: ClassifiedFrame[];\n  groups: FrameGroup[];\n  droppedCount: number;\n}\n\n// NOTE: This dedup compares CONSECUTIVE frames only. Non-consecutive appearances of the\n// same screen (e.g., Screen A at 5:00, Screen B at 20:00, Screen A at 45:00) will NOT be\n// grouped — both go through P1 extraction. A1 assembly merges them later via title-bar\n// grouping, so correctness is preserved, but extra Gemini calls are spent.\n// TODO: Future improvement — cross-group similarity comparison to catch non-consecutive duplicates.\n\n/**\n * Generate a small thumbnail for pixel comparison.\n */\nexport async function generateThumbnail(imagePath: string): Promise<Buffer> {\n  return sharp(imagePath)\n    .resize(64, 64, { fit: 'fill' })\n    .grayscale()\n    .raw()\n    .toBuffer();\n}\n\n/**\n * Calculate normalized pixel difference between two thumbnails.\n * Returns 0.0 (identical) to 1.0 (completely different).\n */\nexport function pixelDifference(thumbA: Buffer, thumbB: Buffer): number {\n  if (thumbA.length !== thumbB.length) return 1.0;\n  let totalDiff = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < thumbA.length; i++) {\n    totalDiff += Math.abs(thumbA[i] - thumbB[i]);\n  }\n  return totalDiff / (thumbA.length * 255);\n}\n\n/**\n * Group consecutive similar screen frames.\n * Similarity threshold: frames with <15% pixel difference are grouped.\n */\nexport async function groupConsecutiveFrames(\n  frames: ClassifiedFrame[],\n  similarityThreshold: number = 0.15,\n): Promise<FrameGroup[]> {\n  if (frames.length === 0) return [];\n\n  const thumbnails = await Promise.all(\n    frames.map(f => generateThumbnail(f.imagePath)),\n  );\n\n  const groups: FrameGroup[] = [];\n  let currentGroup: ClassifiedFrame[] = [frames[0]];\n\n  for (let i = 1; i < frames.length; i++) {\n    const diff = pixelDifference(thumbnails[i - 1], thumbnails[i]);\n    if (diff < similarityThreshold) {\n      currentGroup.push(frames[i]);\n    } else {\n      groups.push({\n        frames: currentGroup,\n        representative: currentGroup[0],\n      });\n      currentGroup = [frames[i]];\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Push final group\n  groups.push({\n    frames: currentGroup,\n    representative: currentGroup[0],\n  });\n\n  return groups;\n}\n\n/**\n * Select 2-3 most visually diverse frames from a group.\n * For groups of 1-3, keep all. For larger groups, pick first, last, and most different from first.\n */\nexport async function selectDiverseFrames(\n  group: FrameGroup,\n  maxSelect: number = 3,\n): Promise<ClassifiedFrame[]> {\n  const { frames } = group;\n  if (frames.length <= maxSelect) return [...frames];\n\n  // Always keep first and last\n  const selected: ClassifiedFrame[] = [frames[0]];\n\n  if (maxSelect >= 3 && frames.length > 2) {\n    // Find the frame most different from the first\n    const firstThumb = await generateThumbnail(frames[0].imagePath);\n    let maxDiff = 0;\n    let mostDifferentIdx = 1;\n\n    for (let i = 1; i < frames.length - 1; i++) {\n      const thumb = await generateThumbnail(frames[i].imagePath);\n      const diff = pixelDifference(firstThumb, thumb);\n      if (diff > maxDiff) {\n        maxDiff = diff;\n        mostDifferentIdx = i;\n      }\n    }\n\n    selected.push(frames[mostDifferentIdx]);\n  }\n\n  selected.push(frames[frames.length - 1]);\n\n  // Deduplicate in case mostDifferent is the last frame\n  const uniquePaths = new Set<string>();\n  return selected.filter(f => {\n    if (uniquePaths.has(f.imagePath)) return false;\n    uniquePaths.add(f.imagePath);\n    return true;\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Main entry point. Groups consecutive similar frames, selects 2-3 per group.\n */\nexport async function deduplicateFrames(\n  screenFrames: ClassifiedFrame[],\n  options?: { similarityThreshold?: number; maxPerGroup?: number },\n): Promise<DedupResult> {\n  const threshold = options?.similarityThreshold ?? 0.15;\n  const maxPerGroup = options?.maxPerGroup ?? 3;\n\n  const groups = await groupConsecutiveFrames(screenFrames, threshold);\n\n  const selectedFrames: ClassifiedFrame[] = [];\n  let droppedCount = 0;\n\n  for (const group of groups) {\n    const selected = await selectDiverseFrames(group, maxPerGroup);\n    selectedFrames.push(...selected);\n    droppedCount += group.frames.length - selected.length;\n  }\n\n  return { selectedFrames, groups, droppedCount };\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-dedup.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **pixelDifference** — identical buffers return 0, completely different buffers return ~1.0, different length buffers return 1.0\n2. **groupConsecutiveFrames** — groups similar consecutive frames together, separates dissimilar frames into different groups, single frame returns one group, empty input returns empty array. Mock `sharp` via `vi.mock('sharp')` to return controlled thumbnail buffers.\n3. **selectDiverseFrames** — keeps all frames for groups of 1-3, selects 3 diverse frames for larger groups, deduplicates if most-different is the last frame\n4. **deduplicateFrames** — full integration: 10 frames with 3 groups → selects 6-9 frames, tracks droppedCount correctly\n5. Verify the NOTE comment about consecutive-only limitation exists in the source file\n\n---\n\n### File 4: `src/lib/pipeline/transcript-context.ts`\n\n```typescript\n// Convention: otterTime = videoTime + offsetSeconds\n// This module uses per-chunk offsets to index into a day-level Otter file.\n// The default case is ONE Otter transcript covering MULTIPLE video chunks.\n// Each chunk has its own offset; this module applies the chunk's offset to\n// find the correct section of the day-level Otter transcript for each frame.\n\nimport type { TranscriptSegment } from './transcript';\n\nexport interface FrameTranscriptContext {\n  imagePath: string;\n  videoTimestamp: number;    // original video timestamp\n  alignedOtterTime: number;  // videoTimestamp + offsetSeconds\n  transcriptSnippet: string; // Otter text ±60s around aligned time\n  speakers: string[];\n}\n\nexport interface ArtifactTranscriptContext {\n  artifactFilename: string;\n  transcriptSnippet: string;\n  matchedKeywords: string[];\n  speakers: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Get transcript context for a single frame.\n * Applies per-chunk offset to convert video timestamp to Otter time,\n * then finds Otter segments within ±windowSeconds of that aligned time.\n *\n * otterSegments: the DAY-LEVEL Otter transcript (one Otter covers all chunks).\n * offsetSeconds: THIS CHUNK's offset (otterTime = videoTime + offsetSeconds).\n */\nexport function getFrameContext(\n  videoTimestamp: number,\n  imagePath: string,\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  offsetSeconds: number,\n  windowSeconds: number = 60,\n): FrameTranscriptContext {\n  const alignedOtterTime = videoTimestamp + offsetSeconds;\n  const windowStart = alignedOtterTime - windowSeconds;\n  const windowEnd = alignedOtterTime + windowSeconds;\n\n  const matchedSegments = otterSegments.filter(\n    seg => seg.startTime < windowEnd && seg.endTime > windowStart,\n  );\n\n  const speakers = [...new Set(\n    matchedSegments.map(s => s.speaker).filter((s): s is string => !!s),\n  )];\n\n  const transcriptSnippet = matchedSegments\n    .map(seg => {\n      const prefix = seg.speaker ? `[${seg.speaker}] ` : '';\n      return `${prefix}${seg.text}`;\n    })\n    .join('\\n');\n\n  return {\n    imagePath,\n    videoTimestamp,\n    alignedOtterTime,\n    transcriptSnippet,\n    speakers,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Get transcript context for all frames from a single video chunk.\n * Uses the chunk's specific offset to align against the day-level Otter transcript.\n */\nexport function getFrameContexts(\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  chunkOffsetSeconds: number,\n  windowSeconds: number = 60,\n): FrameTranscriptContext[] {\n  return frames.map(frame =>\n    getFrameContext(frame.timestamp, frame.imagePath, otterSegments, chunkOffsetSeconds, windowSeconds),\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Get transcript context for an artifact by keyword search.\n * Searches for the artifact name/number in Otter transcript.\n */\nexport function getArtifactContext(\n  artifactFilename: string,\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  additionalKeywords: string[] = [],\n): ArtifactTranscriptContext {\n  // Extract keywords from filename: \"Artifact-1.jpeg\" → [\"artifact\", \"1\"]\n  const filenameKeywords = artifactFilename\n    .replace(/\\.[^.]+$/, '')  // strip extension\n    .split(/[-_\\s]+/)\n    .filter(w => w.length > 0)\n    .map(w => w.toLowerCase());\n\n  const allKeywords = [...filenameKeywords, ...additionalKeywords.map(k => k.toLowerCase())];\n\n  const matchedSegments: TranscriptSegment[] = [];\n  const matchedKeywords: Set<string> = new Set();\n\n  for (const seg of otterSegments) {\n    const lowerText = seg.text.toLowerCase();\n    for (const keyword of allKeywords) {\n      if (lowerText.includes(keyword)) {\n        matchedSegments.push(seg);\n        matchedKeywords.add(keyword);\n        break; // don't double-add the same segment\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  const speakers = [...new Set(\n    matchedSegments.map(s => s.speaker).filter((s): s is string => !!s),\n  )];\n\n  const transcriptSnippet = matchedSegments\n    .map(seg => {\n      const prefix = seg.speaker ? `[${seg.speaker}] ` : '';\n      return `${prefix}${seg.text}`;\n    })\n    .join('\\n');\n\n  return {\n    artifactFilename,\n    transcriptSnippet,\n    matchedKeywords: [...matchedKeywords],\n    speakers,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Format frame transcript context for injection into P1 prompt.\n */\nexport function formatFrameContextForPrompt(context: FrameTranscriptContext): string {\n  if (!context.transcriptSnippet) return '';\n  const speakerInfo = context.speakers.length > 0\n    ? `Speakers: ${context.speakers.join(', ')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  return `\\n## TRANSCRIPT CONTEXT\\n\\nTimestamp alignment: video ${formatTime(context.videoTimestamp)} → Otter ${formatTime(context.alignedOtterTime)}\\n${speakerInfo}\\n${context.transcriptSnippet}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Format artifact transcript context for injection into P2/P3/P4 prompt.\n */\nexport function formatArtifactContextForPrompt(context: ArtifactTranscriptContext): string {\n  if (!context.transcriptSnippet) return '';\n  const kwInfo = context.matchedKeywords.length > 0\n    ? `Matched keywords: ${context.matchedKeywords.join(', ')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  const speakerInfo = context.speakers.length > 0\n    ? `Speakers: ${context.speakers.join(', ')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  return `\\n## TRANSCRIPT CONTEXT\\n\\n${kwInfo}${speakerInfo}\\n${context.transcriptSnippet}`;\n}\n\nfunction formatTime(seconds: number): string {\n  const m = Math.floor(seconds / 60);\n  const s = Math.floor(seconds % 60).toString().padStart(2, '0');\n  return `${m}:${s}`;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/transcript-context.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **getFrameContext** — finds Most common.\nHANDWRITING — A document with significant handwritten content (notes, filled-in forms with handwriting, handwritten annotations that are central to the document's content).\nDENSE_TABLE — A document dominated by a large data table with many rows and columns (spreadsheets, ledgers, pricing matrices, schedules with 10+ rows).\n\nReply in this exact format:\nCLASSIFICATION: [STANDARD|HANDWRITING|DENSE_TABLE]\nCONFIDENCE: [HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW]\nREASONING: [one sentence explaining why]`,\n          },\n        ],\n      },\n    ],\n  });\n\n  return parseClassificationResult(text);\n}\n\nexport function parseClassificationResult(response: string): ClassificationResult {\n  const classMatch = response.match(/CLASSIFICATION:\\s*(STANDARD|HANDWRITING|DENSE_TABLE)/i);\n  const confMatch = response.match(/CONFIDENCE:\\s*(HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW)/i);\n  const reasonMatch = response.match(/REASONING:\\s*(.+)/i);\n\n  const classMap: Record<string, ArtifactClassification> = {\n    'STANDARD': 'artifact_standard',\n    'HANDWRITING': 'artifact_handwriting',\n    'DENSE_TABLE': 'artifact_dense_table',\n  };\n\n  const classification = classMap[classMatch?.[1]?.toUpperCase() ?? 'STANDARD'] ?? 'artifact_standard';\n  const confidenceMap: Record<string, 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'> = {\n    'HIGH': 'high', 'MEDIUM': 'medium', 'LOW': 'low',\n  };\n  const confidence = confidenceMap[confMatch?.[1]?.toUpperCase() ?? 'MEDIUM'] ?? 'medium';\n  const reasoning = reasonMatch?.[1]?.trim() ?? 'No reasoning provided';\n\n  return { classification, confidence, reasoning };\n}\n\n/**\n * Classify multiple artifacts. Returns a map of filename → classification.\n */\nexport async function classifyArtifacts(\n  artifacts: { filename: string; imagePath: string }[],\n): Promise<Map<string, ClassificationResult>> {\n  const results = new Map<string, ClassificationResult>();\n\n  for (const artifact of artifacts) {\n    try {\n      const result = await classifyArtifact(artifact.imagePath);\n      results.set(artifact.filename, result);\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error(`Artifact classification failed for ${artifact.filename}:`, error);\n      // Default to standard on failure\n      results.set(artifact.filename, {\n        classification: 'artifact_standard',\n        confidence: 'low',\n        reasoning: 'Classification failed, defaulting to standard',\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return results;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/artifact-classifier.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **parseClassificationResult** — parses STANDARD correctly, parses HANDWRITING correctly, parses DENSE_TABLE correctly, defaults to standard on unparseable input, parses confidence levels\n2. **classifyArtifact** — mock Gemini call, verify it sends image and correct prompt\n3. **classifyArtifacts** — classifies multiple artifacts, handles individual failures gracefully (defaults to standard)\n\n---\n\n### Change 5: P1 Prompt Update (`src/lib/pipeline/prompts/p1-screen-page.ts`)\n\nAdd after the first line of the prompt (after \"You are processing a single page...\"):\n\n```\nThis image is extracted from a video recording of a software demonstration. User drops all files for a day: video chunks (.mp4), Otter transcript (.txt), VTT files (.vtt), audio (.m4a), artifact photos (.jpeg)\n2. System auto-classifies by extension\n3. For artifacts: Gemini auto-classifies extraction type (standard/handwriting/dense_table) — user can override\n4. System pairs videos with transcripts\n5. Processing:\n   a. Parse all transcripts (Otter + VTT)\n   b. **VIDEO PHASE** per chunk:\n      - ffmpeg scene detection → raw frames (using existing `extractScenes` from extract.ts)\n      - Frame classification (Gemini: screen vs not-screen)\n      - Frame grouping + multi-select (2-3 best per group)\n      - Offset calculation (VTT↔Otter text match, or Gemini visual↔Otter)\n      - Create synthetic batchFiles rows for each selected frame (extractionType: 'screen_frame', with parentVideoFileId, videoTimestamp, chunkIdentifier)\n   c. **ARTIFACT PHASE:**\n      - Auto-classify (Gemini: standard/handwriting/dense_table) — if not already classified by user\n      - Find transcript context for each artifact\n   d. **PER-IMAGE EXTRACTION:**\n      - screen_frame → C1 → P1 (with per-frame transcript context from offset alignment)\n      - artifact_* → C1 → P2/P3/P4 (with artifact transcript context)\n   e. **ASSEMBLY:** A1 (cross-chunk merge via title-bar grouping) → A2 → V1\n   f. Complete\n\n### One Otter covers many chunks\n\nThe default case is ONE Otter transcript covering the entire day. There are typically 3-6 video chunks per day, each with a different start time. The offset calculator produces a per-chunk offset. `transcript-context.ts` uses each chunk's offset to index into the single day-level Otter transcript — this is how you find the right section of Otter for each frame.\n\n### Offset convention\n\n`otterTime = videoTime + offsetSeconds`. Always. Everywhere. Header regex: /^##\\s+Artifact\\s+\\d+:\\s+(.+)$/m — extract artifact name.\n  2. Metadata: Parse **Label:** lines using a helper similar to P1's\n  parseMetadataLine. Labels to parse: Document Type, Source Photo, Original\n  Filename, Orientation, Customer-Facing, Source Screen, Document Set, Data\n  Format. All nullable.\n  3. ### Fields Extracted: Parse the 5-column table (# | Field Label | Value |\n  Type | Extraction Quality). Same row-parsing technique as P1's\n  parseFieldTable, mapping to ArtifactFieldEntry.\n  4. ### Tabular Data: May contain multiple **Table:** blocks within one\n  section. For each block, parse:\n    - **Table:** → tableName\n    - **Columns:** → columns (number)\n    - **Rows:** or **Data Rows:** → rows (number)\n    - **Column Alignment Confidence:** → columnAlignmentConfidence\n    - The markdown table after the metadata: first row with pipe separators is\n  headers, separator row (dashes), then data rows. The last column in each data\n  row is the row-level Extraction Quality flag.\n  5. ### Matrix/Grid Structure (P3 only): Convert to TabularDataSection:\n    - **Extraction Confidence:** → columnAlignmentConfidence\n    - **Matrix Dimensions:** → parse {rows} x {columns} for rows and columns\n    - Parse the matrix table. First column cells are bold row headers (strip **\n  markers). Remaining columns are data cells. Each data cell may contain inline\n  quality flags like [CLEAR] at the end.\n    - Strip inline quality flags from cell values. Aggregate to row-level: the\n  worst quality flag among all cells in a row becomes the row's\n  extractionQuality. Severity order: UNREADABLE > UNCERTAIN > PARTIAL > CLEAR.\n  Default CLEAR if no flag found.\n    - tableName: use the artifact name from the parent entry.\n    - Add observation: \"Original extraction included per-cell quality flags —\n  see source extraction for detail.\"\n  6. ### Supplementary Notes (P3 only): Parse bullet items. Merge into the\n  observations array.\n  7. ### Business Rules Visible: Parse bullet items → businessRules array.\n  8. ### Observations: Parse bullet items → observations array.\n\n  Tests\n\n  Test file: src/lib/pipeline/artifact-output-parser.test.ts\n\n  Test 1: \"parses P2 artifact with metadata and fields\" — Standard P2 output\n  with all metadata lines and a ### Fields Extracted table with 3 rows.      // video timestamp in seconds\n  description: string;    // Gemini-generated description of what's on screen\n  imagePath: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy A: VTT↔Otter text match.\n * Parse both VTT and Otter segments, fuzzy-match text segments (>60% word overlap),\n * calculate offset per match, return median.\n */\nexport function calculateWordOverlap(textA: string, textB: string): number {\n  const wordsA = new Set(textA.toLowerCase().split(/\\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 3));\n  const wordsB = new Set(textB.toLowerCase().split(/\\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 3));\n  if (wordsA.size === 0 || wordsB.size === 0) return 0;\n  const intersection = [...wordsA].filter(w => wordsB.has(w)).length;\n  const minSize = Math.min(wordsA.size, wordsB.size);\n  return intersection / minSize;\n}\n\nexport function strategyA(\n  vttSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n): OffsetResult | null {\n  const matches: number[] = [];\n\n  for (const vtt of vttSegments) {\n    for (const otter of otterSegments) {\n      const overlap = calculateWordOverlap(vtt.text, otter.text);\n      if (overlap >= 0.6) {\n        // offset = otterTime - videoTime\n        matches.push(otter.startTime - vtt.startTime);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (matches.length < 3) return null;\n\n  matches.sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const median = matches[Math.floor(matches.length / 2)];\n  const variance = matches.reduce((sum, m) => sum + Math.abs(m - median), 0) / matches.length;\n\n  return {\n    offsetSeconds: median,\n    confidence: variance < 5 ? 'high' : variance < 15 ? 'medium' : 'low',\n    strategy: 'vtt_text_match',\n    matchCount: matches.length,\n    varianceSeconds: variance,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy B: Gemini visual↔Otter keyword match.\n * Pick scene-change frames, get Gemini descriptions, search Otter for keywords,\n * calculate offset from matches.\n *\n * frameDescriptions: pre-classified frames with Gemini descriptions (from frame-classifier).\n * otterSegments: parsed Otter transcript.\n */\nexport function strategyB(\n  frameDescriptions: FrameDescription[],\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n): OffsetResult | null {\n  // Pick up to 5 well-spaced frames\n  const picked = pickSpacedFrames(frameDescriptions, 5);\n  if (picked.length === 0) return null;\n\n  const matches: number[] = [];\n\n  for (const frame of picked) {\n    // Extract keywords from Gemini description (nouns, app-specific terms)\n    const keywords = extractKeywords(frame.description);\n    if (keywords.length === 0) continue;\n\n    // Find best matching Otter segment\n    let bestScore = 0;\n    let bestOtterTime = 0;\n    for (const otter of otterSegments) {\n      const score = keywords.filter(kw =>\n        otter.text.toLowerCase().includes(kw.toLowerCase())\n      ).length / keywords.length;\n      if (score > bestScore) {\n        bestScore = score;\n        bestOtterTime = otter.startTime;\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (bestScore >= 0.3) {\n      matches.push(bestOtterTime - frame.timestamp);\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (matches.length < 2) return null;\n\n  matches.sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const median = matches[Math.floor(matches.length / 2)];\n  const variance = matches.reduce((sum, m) => sum + Math.abs(m - median), 0) / matches.length;\n\n  return {\n    offsetSeconds: median,\n    confidence: variance < 10 ? 'high' : variance < 30 ? 'medium' : 'low',\n    strategy: 'gemini_visual_match',\n    matchCount: matches.length,\n    varianceSeconds: variance,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy C: Manual entry fallback.\n */\nexport function strategyManual(offsetSeconds: number): OffsetResult {\n  return {\n    offsetSeconds,\n    confidence: 'high',\n    strategy: 'manual',\n    matchCount: 0,\n    varianceSeconds: 0,\n  };\n}\n\nexport function pickSpacedFrames(frames: FrameDescription[], count: number): FrameDescription[] {\n  if (frames.length <= count) return frames;\n  const step = frames.length / count;\n  const picked: FrameDescription[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n    picked.push(frames[Math.floor(i * step)]);\n  }\n  return picked;\n}\n\nexport function extractKeywords(description: string): string[] {\n  // Extract meaningful words (4+ chars, not common stop words)\n  const stopWords = new Set([\n    'this', 'that', 'with', 'from', 'have', 'been', 'were', 'they',\n    'will', 'would', 'could', 'should', 'there', 'their', 'about',\n    'which', 'when', 'what', 'some', 'other', 'than', 'then', 'also',\n    'just', 'more', 'very', 'into', 'over', 'such', 'after', 'before',\n    'between', 'each', 'being', 'does', 'doing', 'during', 'having',\n    'image', 'shows', 'showing', 'screen', 'appears', 'displayed',\n    'visible', 'window', 'application',\n  ]);\n  return description\n    .split(/[\\s,;:.!?()]+/)\n    .filter(w => w.length >= 4 && !stopWords.has(w.toLowerCase()))\n    .map(w => w.toLowerCase());\n}\n\n/**\n * Main entry point. Tries strategies in order: A → B → null (caller should prompt for manual).\n */\nexport async function calculateOffset(\n  vttSegments: TranscriptSegment[] | null,\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  frameDescriptions: FrameDescription[],\n): Promise<OffsetResult | null> {\n  // Strategy A: VTT↔Otter text match (fastest, most accurate when VTT available)\n  if (vttSegments && vttSegments.length > 0) {\n    const resultA = strategyA(vttSegments, otterSegments);\n    if (resultA && resultA.confidence !== 'low') {\n      return resultA;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Strategy B: Gemini visual↔Otter keyword match\n  if (frameDescriptions.length > 0 && otterSegments.length > 0) {\n    const resultB = strategyB(frameDescriptions, otterSegments);\n    if (resultB) {\n      return resultB;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // No automated strategy produced confident result\n  return null;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/offset-calculator.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **calculateWordOverlap** — 100% overlap returns 1.0, 0% returns 0, partial returns correct ratio, ignores short words (<4 chars)\n2. **strategyA** — returns high-confidence result when 5+ VTT/Otter segments match with >60% overlap, returns null with fewer than 3 matches, calculates correct median offset, variance reflects spread\n3. **strategyB** — returns result when keywords match Otter segments, returns null when no keywords match, picks spaced frames correctly\n4. **pickSpacedFrames** — returns all frames if count >= frames.length, picks evenly spaced frames otherwise\n5. **extractKeywords** — filters stop words, filters short words, lowercases\n6. **calculateOffset** — tries strategy A first when VTT available, falls back to B when A returns null, falls back to B when A returns low confidence, returns null when both fail, skips A when no VTT segments\n7. **strategyManual** — returns correct result with high confidence and manual strategy\n\nUse mock TranscriptSegment data — do NOT read real files in unit tests.       // video timestamp in seconds\n  isScreen: boolean;\n  description: string;     // Gemini description — reused for offset calculation\n  filterReason?: string;   // 'face' | 'transition' | 'blank' | 'other' if not a screen\n}\n\n/**\n * Classify a batch of frames using Gemini.\n * Batches 4-6 frames at a time to reduce API calls.\n * Returns classification + description for each frame.\n */\nexport async function classifyFrames(\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n  batchSize: number = 4,\n): Promise<ClassifiedFrame[]> {\n  const results: ClassifiedFrame[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < frames.length; i += batchSize) {\n    const batch = frames.slice(i, i + batchSize);\n    const batchResults = await classifyBatch(batch);\n    results.push(...batchResults);\n  }\n\n  return results;\n}\n\nexport async function classifyBatch(\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n): Promise<ClassifiedFrame[]> {\n  const fileParts = await Promise.all(\n    frames.map(async (frame) => {\n      const data = await readFile(frame.imagePath);\n      const mediaType = detectMediaType(frame.imagePath);\n      return { type: 'file' as const, data, mediaType };\n    }),\n  );\n\n  const prompt = `You are classifying ${frames.length} video frames. For EACH frame (numbered 1 to ${frames.length}), determine:\n\n1. Is this a software application screen? (Yes/No)\n2. Brief description of what's shown (10-20 words)\n3. If not a software screen, why? (face/transition/blank/other)\n\nA \"software application screen\" means a desktop or web application UI with forms, fields, menus, buttons, or data grids. Zoom meeting participant video, webcam feeds, desktop backgrounds, and loading screens are NOT software screens.\n\nReply in this exact format, one line per frame:\nFRAME 1: [YES|NO] | [description] | [reason if NO]\nFRAME 2: [YES|NO] | [description] | [reason if NO]\n...`;\n\n  const { text } = await generateText({\n    model: google('gemini-2.5-flash'),\n    messages: [\n      {\n        role: 'user',\n        content: [\n          ...fileParts,\n          { type: 'text', text: prompt },\n        ],\n      },\n    ],\n  });\n\n  return parseClassificationResponse(text, frames);\n}\n\nexport function parseClassificationResponse(\n  response: string,\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n): ClassifiedFrame[] {\n  const lines = response.split('\\n').filter(l => l.trim().startsWith('FRAME'));\n  const results: ClassifiedFrame[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = 0; i < frames.length; i++) {\n    const line = lines[i];\n    if (!line) {\n      // Default to keeping unclassified frames as screens (conservative)\n      results.push({\n        imagePath: frames[i].imagePath,\n        timestamp: frames[i].timestamp,\n        isScreen: true,\n        description: 'Classification unavailable',\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    const parts = line.split('|').map(p => p.trim());\n    const isScreen = parts[0]?.toUpperCase().includes('YES') ?? false;\n    const description = parts[1] || 'No description';\n    const filterReason = !isScreen ? (parts[2] || 'other') : undefined;\n\n    results.push({\n      imagePath: frames[i].imagePath,\n      timestamp: frames[i].timestamp,\n      isScreen,\n      description,\n      filterReason,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return results;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-classifier.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **parseClassificationResponse** — parses YES responses correctly, parses NO responses with filter reason, handles missing lines (defaults to isScreen=true), handles empty response\n2. **classifyFrames** — batches correctly (10 frames with batchSize=4 → 3 batches), passes frames to classifyBatch\n3. Mock the Gemini call in classifyBatch — vi.mock `@ai-sdk/google` and `ai` as done in existing tests\n\n---\n\n### File 3: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-dedup.ts`\n\n```typescript\nimport sharp from 'sharp';\nimport type { ClassifiedFrame } from './frame-classifier';\n\nexport interface FrameGroup {\n  frames: ClassifiedFrame[];\n  representative: ClassifiedFrame;  // first frame in group\n}\n\nexport interface DedupResult {\n  selectedFrames: ClassifiedFrame[];\n  groups: FrameGroup[];\n  droppedCount: number;\n}\n\n// NOTE: This dedup compares CONSECUTIVE frames only. Non-consecutive appearances of the\n// same screen (e.g., Screen A at 5:00, Screen B at 20:00, Screen A at 45:00) will NOT be\n// grouped — both go through P1 extraction. A1 assembly merges them later via title-bar\n// grouping, so correctness is preserved, but extra Gemini calls are spent.\n// TODO: Future improvement — cross-group similarity comparison to catch non-consecutive duplicates.\n\n/**\n * Generate a small thumbnail for pixel comparison.\n */\nexport async function generateThumbnail(imagePath: string): Promise<Buffer> {\n  return sharp(imagePath)\n    .resize(64, 64, { fit: 'fill' })\n    .grayscale()\n    .raw()\n    .toBuffer();\n}\n\n/**\n * Calculate normalized pixel difference between two thumbnails.\n * Returns 0.0 (identical) to 1.0 (completely different).\n */\nexport function pixelDifference(thumbA: Buffer, thumbB: Buffer): number {\n  if (thumbA.length !== thumbB.length) return 1.0;\n  let totalDiff = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < thumbA.length; i++) {\n    totalDiff += Math.abs(thumbA[i] - thumbB[i]);\n  }\n  return totalDiff / (thumbA.length * 255);\n}\n\n/**\n * Group consecutive similar screen frames.\n * Similarity threshold: frames with <15% pixel difference are grouped.\n */\nexport async function groupConsecutiveFrames(\n  frames: ClassifiedFrame[],\n  similarityThreshold: number = 0.15,\n): Promise<FrameGroup[]> {\n  if (frames.length === 0) return [];\n\n  const thumbnails = await Promise.all(\n    frames.map(f => generateThumbnail(f.imagePath)),\n  );\n\n  const groups: FrameGroup[] = [];\n  let currentGroup: ClassifiedFrame[] = [frames[0]];\n\n  for (let i = 1; i < frames.length; i++) {\n    const diff = pixelDifference(thumbnails[i - 1], thumbnails[i]);\n    if (diff < similarityThreshold) {\n      currentGroup.push(frames[i]);\n    } else {\n      groups.push({\n        frames: currentGroup,\n        representative: currentGroup[0],\n      });\n      currentGroup = [frames[i]];\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Push final group\n  groups.push({\n    frames: currentGroup,\n    representative: currentGroup[0],\n  });\n\n  return groups;\n}\n\n/**\n * Select 2-3 most visually diverse frames from a group.\n * For groups of 1-3, keep all. For larger groups, pick first, last, and most different from first.\n */\nexport async function selectDiverseFrames(\n  group: FrameGroup,\n  maxSelect: number = 3,\n): Promise<ClassifiedFrame[]> {\n  const { frames } = group;\n  if (frames.length <= maxSelect) return [...frames];\n\n  // Always keep first and last\n  const selected: ClassifiedFrame[] = [frames[0]];\n\n  if (maxSelect >= 3 && frames.length > 2) {\n    // Find the frame most different from the first\n    const firstThumb = await generateThumbnail(frames[0].imagePath);\n    let maxDiff = 0;\n    let mostDifferentIdx = 1;\n\n    for (let i = 1; i < frames.length - 1; i++) {\n      const thumb = await generateThumbnail(frames[i].imagePath);\n      const diff = pixelDifference(firstThumb, thumb);\n      if (diff > maxDiff) {\n        maxDiff = diff;\n        mostDifferentIdx = i;\n      }\n    }\n\n    selected.push(frames[mostDifferentIdx]);\n  }\n\n  selected.push(frames[frames.length - 1]);\n\n  // Deduplicate in case mostDifferent is the last frame\n  const uniquePaths = new Set<string>();\n  return selected.filter(f => {\n    if (uniquePaths.has(f.imagePath)) return false;\n    uniquePaths.add(f.imagePath);\n    return true;\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Main entry point. Groups consecutive similar frames, selects 2-3 per group.\n */\nexport async function deduplicateFrames(\n  screenFrames: ClassifiedFrame[],\n  options?: { similarityThreshold?: number; maxPerGroup?: number },\n): Promise<DedupResult> {\n  const threshold = options?.similarityThreshold ?? 0.15;\n  const maxPerGroup = options?.maxPerGroup ?? 3;\n\n  const groups = await groupConsecutiveFrames(screenFrames, threshold);\n\n  const selectedFrames: ClassifiedFrame[] = [];\n  let droppedCount = 0;\n\n  for (const group of groups) {\n    const selected = await selectDiverseFrames(group, maxPerGroup);\n    selectedFrames.push(...selected);\n    droppedCount += group.frames.length - selected.length;\n  }\n\n  return { selectedFrames, groups, droppedCount };\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/frame-dedup.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **pixelDifference** — identical buffers return 0, completely different buffers return ~1.0, different length buffers return 1.0\n2. **groupConsecutiveFrames** — groups similar consecutive frames together, separates dissimilar frames into different groups, single frame returns one group, empty input returns empty array. Mock `sharp` via `vi.mock('sharp')` to return controlled thumbnail buffers.\n3. **selectDiverseFrames** — keeps all frames for groups of 1-3, selects 3 diverse frames for larger groups, deduplicates if most-different is the last frame\n4. **deduplicateFrames** — full integration: 10 frames with 3 groups → selects 6-9 frames, tracks droppedCount correctly\n5. videoTime + offsetSeconds\n// This module uses per-chunk offsets to index into a day-level Otter file.\n// The default case is ONE Otter transcript covering MULTIPLE video chunks.\n// Each chunk has its own offset; this module applies the chunk's offset to\n// find the correct section of the day-level Otter transcript for each frame.\n\nimport type { TranscriptSegment } from './transcript';\n\nexport interface FrameTranscriptContext {\n  imagePath: string;\n  videoTimestamp: number;    // original video timestamp\n  alignedOtterTime: number;  // videoTimestamp + offsetSeconds\n  transcriptSnippet: string; // Otter text ±60s around aligned time\n  speakers: string[];\n}\n\nexport interface ArtifactTranscriptContext {\n  artifactFilename: string;\n  transcriptSnippet: string;\n  matchedKeywords: string[];\n  speakers: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Get transcript context for a single frame.\n * Applies per-chunk offset to convert video timestamp to Otter time,\n * then finds Otter segments within ±windowSeconds of that aligned time.\n *\n * otterSegments: the DAY-LEVEL Otter transcript (one Otter covers all chunks).\n * offsetSeconds: THIS CHUNK's offset (otterTime = videoTime + offsetSeconds).\n */\nexport function getFrameContext(\n  videoTimestamp: number,\n  imagePath: string,\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  offsetSeconds: number,\n  windowSeconds: number = 60,\n): FrameTranscriptContext {\n  const alignedOtterTime = videoTimestamp + offsetSeconds;\n  const windowStart = alignedOtterTime - windowSeconds;\n  const windowEnd = alignedOtterTime + windowSeconds;\n\n  const matchedSegments = otterSegments.filter(\n    seg => seg.startTime < windowEnd && seg.endTime > windowStart,\n  );\n\n  const speakers = [...new Set(\n    matchedSegments.map(s => s.speaker).filter((s): s is string => !!s),\n  )];\n\n  const transcriptSnippet = matchedSegments\n    .map(seg => {\n      const prefix = seg.speaker ? `[${seg.speaker}] ` : '';\n      return `${prefix}${seg.text}`;\n    })\n    .join('\\n');\n\n  return {\n    imagePath,\n    videoTimestamp,\n    alignedOtterTime,\n    transcriptSnippet,\n    speakers,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Get transcript context for all frames from a single video chunk.\n * Uses the chunk's specific offset to align against the day-level Otter transcript.\n */\nexport function getFrameContexts(\n  frames: { imagePath: string; timestamp: number }[],\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  chunkOffsetSeconds: number,\n  windowSeconds: number = 60,\n): FrameTranscriptContext[] {\n  return frames.map(frame =>\n    getFrameContext(frame.timestamp, frame.imagePath, otterSegments, chunkOffsetSeconds, windowSeconds),\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Get transcript context for an artifact by keyword search.\n * Searches for the artifact name/number in Otter transcript.\n */\nexport function getArtifactContext(\n  artifactFilename: string,\n  otterSegments: TranscriptSegment[],\n  additionalKeywords: string[] = [],\n): ArtifactTranscriptContext {\n  // Extract keywords from filename: \"Artifact-1.jpeg\" → [\"artifact\", \"1\"]\n  const filenameKeywords = artifactFilename\n    .replace(/\\.[^.]+$/, '')  // strip extension\n    .split(/[-_\\s]+/)\n    .filter(w => w.length > 0)\n    .map(w => w.toLowerCase());\n\n  const allKeywords = [...filenameKeywords, ...additionalKeywords.map(k => k.toLowerCase())];\n\n  const matchedSegments: TranscriptSegment[] = [];\n  const matchedKeywords: Set<string> = new Set();\n\n  for (const seg of otterSegments) {\n    const lowerText = seg.text.toLowerCase();\n    for (const keyword of allKeywords) {\n      if (lowerText.includes(keyword)) {\n        matchedSegments.push(seg);\n        matchedKeywords.add(keyword);\n        break; // don't double-add the same segment\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  const speakers = [...new Set(\n    matchedSegments.map(s => s.speaker).filter((s): s is string => !!s),\n  )];\n\n  const transcriptSnippet = matchedSegments\n    .map(seg => {\n      const prefix = seg.speaker ? `[${seg.speaker}] ` : '';\n      return `${prefix}${seg.text}`;\n    })\n    .join('\\n');\n\n  return {\n    artifactFilename,\n    transcriptSnippet,\n    matchedKeywords: [...matchedKeywords],\n    speakers,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Format frame transcript context for injection into P1 prompt.\n */\nexport function formatFrameContextForPrompt(context: FrameTranscriptContext): string {\n  if (!context.transcriptSnippet) return '';\n  const speakerInfo = context.speakers.length > 0\n    ? `Speakers: ${context.speakers.join(', ')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  return `\\n## TRANSCRIPT CONTEXT\\n\\nTimestamp alignment: video ${formatTime(context.videoTimestamp)} → Otter ${formatTime(context.alignedOtterTime)}\\n${speakerInfo}\\n${context.transcriptSnippet}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Format artifact transcript context for injection into P2/P3/P4 prompt.\n */\nexport function formatArtifactContextForPrompt(context: ArtifactTranscriptContext): string {\n  if (!context.transcriptSnippet) return '';\n  const kwInfo = context.matchedKeywords.length > 0\n    ? `Matched keywords: ${context.matchedKeywords.join(', ')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  const speakerInfo = context.speakers.length > 0\n    ? `Speakers: ${context.speakers.join(', ')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  return `\\n## TRANSCRIPT CONTEXT\\n\\n${kwInfo}${speakerInfo}\\n${context.transcriptSnippet}`;\n}\n\nfunction formatTime(seconds: number): string {\n  const m = Math.floor(seconds / 60);\n  const s = Math.floor(seconds % 60).toString().padStart(2, '0');\n  return `${m}:${s}`;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/transcript-context.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **getFrameContext** — finds Most common.\nHANDWRITING — A document with significant handwritten content (notes, filled-in forms with handwriting, handwritten annotations that are central to the document's content).\nDENSE_TABLE — A document dominated by a large data table with many rows and columns (spreadsheets, ledgers, pricing matrices, schedules with 10+ rows).\n\nReply in this exact format:\nCLASSIFICATION: [STANDARD|HANDWRITING|DENSE_TABLE]\nCONFIDENCE: [HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW]\nREASONING: [one sentence explaining why]`,\n          },\n        ],\n      },\n    ],\n  });\n\n  return parseClassificationResult(text);\n}\n\nexport function parseClassificationResult(response: string): ClassificationResult {\n  const classMatch = response.match(/CLASSIFICATION:\\s*(STANDARD|HANDWRITING|DENSE_TABLE)/i);\n  const confMatch = response.match(/CONFIDENCE:\\s*(HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW)/i);\n  const reasonMatch = response.match(/REASONING:\\s*(.+)/i);\n\n  const classMap: Record<string, ArtifactClassification> = {\n    'STANDARD': 'artifact_standard',\n    'HANDWRITING': 'artifact_handwriting',\n    'DENSE_TABLE': 'artifact_dense_table',\n  };\n\n  const classification = classMap[classMatch?.[1]?.toUpperCase() ?? 'STANDARD'] ?? 'artifact_standard';\n  const confidenceMap: Record<string, 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'> = {\n    'HIGH': 'high', 'MEDIUM': 'medium', 'LOW': 'low',\n  };\n  const confidence = confidenceMap[confMatch?.[1]?.toUpperCase() ?? 'MEDIUM'] ?? 'medium';\n  const reasoning = reasonMatch?.[1]?.trim() ?? 'No reasoning provided';\n\n  return { classification, confidence, reasoning };\n}\n\n/**\n * Classify multiple artifacts. Returns a map of filename → classification.\n */\nexport async function classifyArtifacts(\n  artifacts: { filename: string; imagePath: string }[],\n): Promise<Map<string, ClassificationResult>> {\n  const results = new Map<string, ClassificationResult>();\n\n  for (const artifact of artifacts) {\n    try {\n      const result = await classifyArtifact(artifact.imagePath);\n      results.set(artifact.filename, result);\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error(`Artifact classification failed for ${artifact.filename}:`, error);\n      // Default to standard on failure\n      results.set(artifact.filename, {\n        classification: 'artifact_standard',\n        confidence: 'low',\n        reasoning: 'Classification failed, defaulting to standard',\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  return results;\n}\n```\n\n#### Tests: `src/lib/pipeline/artifact-classifier.test.ts`\n\nTest cases:\n1. **parseClassificationResult** — parses STANDARD correctly, parses HANDWRITING correctly, parses DENSE_TABLE correctly, defaults to standard on unparseable input, parses confidence levels\n2. **classifyArtifact** — mock Gemini call, verify it sends image and correct prompt\n3. **classifyArtifacts** — classifies multiple artifacts, handles individual failures gracefully (defaults to standard)\n\n---\n\n### Change 5: P1 Prompt Update (`src/lib/pipeline/prompts/p1-screen-page.ts`)\n\nAdd after the first line of the prompt (after \"You are processing a single page...\"):\n\n```\nThis image is extracted from a video recording of a software demonstration. User drops all files for a day: video chunks (.mp4), Otter transcript (.txt), VTT files (.vtt), audio (.m4a), artifact photos (.jpeg)\n2. System auto-classifies by extension\n3. For artifacts: Gemini auto-classifies extraction type (standard/handwriting/dense_table) — user can override\n4. System pairs videos with transcripts\n5. Processing:\n   a. Parse all transcripts (Otter + VTT)\n   b. **VIDEO PHASE** per chunk:\n      - ffmpeg scene detection → raw frames (using existing `extractScenes` from extract.ts)\n      - Frame classification (Gemini: screen vs not-screen)\n      - Frame grouping + multi-select (2-3 best per group)\n      - Offset calculation (VTT↔Otter text match, or Gemini visual↔Otter)\n      - Create synthetic batchFiles rows for each selected frame (extractionType: 'screen_frame', with parentVideoFileId, videoTimestamp, chunkIdentifier)\n   c. **ARTIFACT PHASE:**\n      - Auto-classify (Gemini: standard/handwriting/dense_table) — if not already classified by user\n      - Find transcript context for each artifact\n   d. **PER-IMAGE EXTRACTION:**\n      - screen_frame → C1 → P1 (with per-frame transcript context from offset alignment)\n      - artifact_* → C1 → P2/P3/P4 (with artifact transcript context)\n   e. **ASSEMBLY:** A1 (cross-chunk merge via title-bar grouping) → A2 → V1\n   f. Complete\n\n### One Otter covers many chunks\n\nThe default case is ONE Otter transcript covering the entire day. There are typically 3-6 video chunks per day, each with a different start time. The offset calculator produces a per-chunk offset. `transcript-context.ts` uses each chunk's offset to index into the single day-level Otter transcript — this is how you find the right section of Otter for each frame.\n\n### Offset convention\n\n`otterTime = videoTime + offsetSeconds`. Always. Everywhere. The offset is positive when Otter started before video.\n\n### Existing code that stays\n\n- `extractScenes` from `extract.ts` — already does ffmpeg scene detection, returns `{ timestamps, screenshotPaths }`\n- `correctRotation` from `rotation-corrector.ts` — C1, works on any image\n- `analyzeImages` from `analyze.ts` — Gemini extraction, already handles transcript/screen/project context\n- `assembleScreenCatalog` from `screen-assembler.ts` — A1, already merges by title bar\n- `assembleArtifactCatalog` from `artifact-assembler.ts` — A2, already handles document sets\n- `validateOutputs` from `output-validator.ts` — V1, already reads filesystem catalogs\n- `parseTranscript` from `transcript.ts` — already handles VTT, SRT, and Otter .txt\n\n---\n\n### Change 1: `src/lib/pipeline/batch-worker.ts` — Full Restructure\n\nThe current batch-worker handles per-image extraction with PDF splitting. Create src/lib/pipeline/p1-output-parser.ts:\n\n  This file parses P1 extraction outputs, which follow the architecture spec\n  §Output File 1 per-screen format. This format is DIFFERENT from what\n  catalog-parser.ts handles — P1 uses ## headers and includes Extraction Quality\n   columns.\n\n  Define the ParsedP1Screen type:\n  export interface P1Field {\n    seq: number;\n    label: string;\n    type: string;\n    currentValue: string;\n    extractionQuality: string;\n  }\n\n  export interface P1GridColumn {\n    seq: number;\n    header: string;\n    type: string;\n    sampleValues: string;\n    extractionQuality: string;\n  }\n\n  export interface P1Grid {\n    name: string;\n    columns: P1GridColumn[];\n    visibleRows: number | null;\n    scrollIndicator: boolean | null;\n  }\n\n  export interface P1Button {\n    seq: number;\n    label: string;\n    position: string;\n    extractionQuality: string;\n  }\n\n  export interface ParsedP1Screen {\n    screenTitle: string;\n    formName: string | null;\n    source: string | null;\n    navigationPath: string | null;\n    parentForm: string | null;\n    possibleDuplicateOf: string | null;\n    headerFields: P1Field[];\n    grids: P1Grid[];\n    tabs: { activeTab: string; otherTabs: string[] } | null;\n    buttons: P1Button[];\n    observations: string[];\n  }\n\n  Export these functions:\n\n  - parseP1Output(rawOutput: string): ParsedP1Screen — Parse a single P1 output\n  string into structured data.\n    - Screen header regex: /^##\\s+Screen\\s+\\d+:\\s+(.+?)(?:\\s+\\((.+)\\))?\\s*$/m —\n  captures title (group 1) and optional form name in parentheses (group 2).\n    - Extract metadata fields: **Source:**, **Navigation Path:**, **Parent\n  Form:** (optional), **Possible Duplicate Of:** (optional). Use pattern\n  \\*\\*{Label}:\\*\\*\\s*(.+).\n    - Parse ### Header Fields table: columns are # | Field Label | Type |\n  Current Value | Extraction Quality. Build P1Field[].\n    - Parse ### Grid: {name} sections: columns are # | Column Header | Type |\n  Sample Values | Extraction Quality. Also extract **Visible Rows:** and\n  **Scroll Indicator:** below the table. Build P1Grid[].\n    - Parse ### Tabs section if present: extract **Active Tab:** and **Other\n  Tabs Visible:**. Also parse any #### Tab: {Label} subsections containing\n  per-tab field tables. Include these tab-specific fields in headerFields — tag\n  them for tab attribution (add a helper note or handle in the assembler).\n    - Parse ### Buttons & Actions table: columns are # | Button Label | Position\n   | Extraction Quality. Build P1Button[].\n    - Parse ### Observations section: collect all -  bullet lines. Build\n  string[].\n  - parseP1Outputs(rawOutputs: string[]): ParsedP1Screen[] — Parse an array of\n  P1 output strings, returning one ParsedP1Screen per output.\n\n  Use relative imports. No @/ aliases.\n\n  Step 2. Create src/lib/pipeline/screen-assembler.ts:\n\n  This file implements A1 from the architecture spec — Screen Catalog Assembly.\n  Import types from ./p1-output-parser. Use relative imports throughout.\n\n  Define the AssembledScreen type:\n  export interface AssembledScreen {\n    screenTitle: string;\n    formName: string | null;\n    source: string | null;\n    navigationPath: string | null;\n    parentForm: string | null;\n    possibleDuplicateOf: string | null;\n    headerFields: P1Field[];          // common fields (visible on all tabs)\n    tabSections: {                     // tab-specific fields\n      tabLabel: string;\n      fields: P1Field[];\n    }[];\n    grids: P1Grid[];\n    tabs: { activeTab: string | null; otherTabs: string[] } | null;\n    buttons: P1Button[];\n    observations: string[];\n  }\n\n  Export these functions:\n\n  - getOutputDir(dayNumber: number): string — Returns\n  data/outputs/day${dayNumber}/. Creates the directory recursively (mkdir -p via\n   mkdirSync with { recursive: true }) if it doesn't exist. This is the local\n  output path for assembled catalogs. V1 will import this function to find\n  output files.\n  - groupByTitleBar(screens: ParsedP1Screen[]): Map<string, ParsedP1Screen[]> —\n  Groups screens by exact screenTitle match. Returns a Map where each key is a\n  title and value is the array of screens sharing that title.\n  - mergeTabEntries(screens: ParsedP1Screen[]): AssembledScreen — Takes an array\n   of P1 outputs with the same title bar (same form, different tabs). Logic:\n    a. All inputs share the same screenTitle (caller guarantees this).\n    b. Collect all unique activeTab values across inputs.\n    c. Build a set of field labels for each input.\n    d. Common fields: field labels that appear in ALL inputs. These go in\n  headerFields.\n    e. Tab-specific fields: field labels that appear in only SOME inputs. For\n  each input that has tab-specific fields, create a tabSections entry with\n  tabLabel = that input's activeTab and fields = the tab-specific fields from\n  that input.\n    f. If an input has no tabs data (no active tab label), use 'Unknown Tab' as\n  the tab label for its unique fields.\n    g. Buttons: union across all inputs, deduplicate by label text\n  (case-insensitive).\n    h. Grids: union across all inputs, deduplicate by grid name\n  (case-insensitive).\n    i. Observations: union across all inputs, deduplicate by trimmed text.\n    j. tabs: set activeTab to the first input's active tab, otherTabs to all\n  other unique tab labels.\n    k. Use the first input's metadata (source, navigationPath, formName) as\n  defaults.\n\n  If only one input is passed (no merge needed), convert it directly to\n  AssembledScreen with empty tabSections.\n  - splitDialogEntry(screen: ParsedP1Screen): { dialog: AssembledScreen;\n  underlyingForm: AssembledScreen } — Called when a P1 output has parentForm set\n   (indicating a dialog over a form).\n\n  - Strategy:\n    a. Parse observations for dialog field attribution cues. Look for patterns:\n        - Lines containing \"dialog\" AND field names (e.g., \"Dialog fields:\n  Field1, Field2\" or \"Fields belonging to the dialog: ...\")\n      - Lines containing \"underlying\" or the parentForm name AND field names\n      - Lines mentioning \"obscured by dialog\" or \"obscured by the dialog\"\n    b. Build two sets of field labels: dialogFieldLabels and formFieldLabels\n  from the observation cues.\n    c. Categorize each headerField:\n        - If its label appears in dialogFieldLabels → assign to dialog entry\n      - If its label appears in formFieldLabels → assign to underlying form\n  entry\n      - If its extractionQuality is [PARTIAL] and observations mention\n  dialog-caused obscuring → assign to underlying form entry\n      - If unattributed and [CLEAR] → assign to dialog entry (the dialog is\n  what's clearly visible in the foreground)\n      - If unattributed and [PARTIAL] without dialog-specific notes → assign to\n  underlying form entry (conservative: [PARTIAL] likely means behind the dialog)\n    d. Dialog entry: screenTitle from the original entry, parentForm preserved.\n  Gets the dialog-assigned fields.\n    e. Underlying form entry: screenTitle = parentForm value. Gets the\n  form-assigned fields. Add observation: \"Partially obscured by dialog — field\n  inventory may be incomplete.\"\n    f. If observations don't contain enough structured cues to confidently split\n   (neither dialogFieldLabels nor formFieldLabels have any entries), fall back\n  to quality-based split: all [CLEAR] fields → dialog, all [PARTIAL] fields →\n  underlying form. Add observation: \"Dialog/form field attribution based on\n  extraction quality flags — may need verification.\"\n    g. Grids: assign to whichever entry seems appropriate based on observation\n  cues, or keep with the dialog entry by default.\n    h. Buttons: assign all to dialog entry (dialog buttons are what's\n  interactive in the foreground).\n  - calculateFieldOverlap(a: ParsedP1Screen, b: ParsedP1Screen): number —\n  Returns 0-1. Logic:\n  labelsA = Set(a.headerFields.map(f => f.label.toLowerCase().trim()))\n  labelsB = Set(b.headerFields.map(f => f.label.toLowerCase().trim()))\n  intersection = labelsA ∩ labelsB\n  return intersection.size / Math.min(labelsA.size, labelsB.size)\n  - Returns 0 if either set is empty.\n  - resolveAmbiguousDedup(screenA: ParsedP1Screen, screenB: ParsedP1Screen):\n  Promise<boolean> — For the 40-60% overlap case with uncertain title bars.\n  Makes a single Gemini call via generateText from 'ai' with\n  google('gemini-2.5-pro') from '@ai-sdk/google'. Text-only (no images).\n\n  - Prompt:\n  These two screen entries have similar field lists but uncertain title bars.\n  Based on the field labels, types, and values shown, do these represent the\n  same application form? Reply with only: yes or no.\n\n  --- Entry A ---\n  Title: {screenA.screenTitle}\n  Fields:\n  {screenA.headerFields.map(f => `- ${f.label} (${f.type}):\n  ${f.currentValue}`).join('\\n')}\n\n  --- Entry B ---\n  Title: {screenB.screenTitle}\n  Fields:\n  {screenB.headerFields.map(f => `- ${f.label} (${f.type}):\n  ${f.currentValue}`).join('\\n')}\n\n  - Parse response: if it contains \"yes\" (case-insensitive), return true\n  (merge). Otherwise return false (keep separate). On any error (Gemini\n  failure), return false (keep separate — conservative default).\n  - assembledScreenToParsedScreen(screen: AssembledScreen, batchId: number):\n  ParsedScreen — Adapter that converts A1's AssembledScreen to the registry's\n  ParsedScreen type (from src/lib/registry/types.ts). Import ParsedScreen,\n  ScreenField, ScreenButton, ScreenGrid from '../registry/types'.\n\n  - Mapping:\n    - screenName ← screen.screenTitle\n    - formName ← screen.formName\n    - applicationContext ← '' (A1 doesn't determine this)\n    - module ← null (modules assigned by EC_1.1B, not project-discovery)\n    - navigationPath ← screen.navigationPath\n    - screenshotSource ← screen.source\n    - fields ← screen.headerFields.map((f, i) => ({ seq: i + 1, label: f.label,\n  type: f.type, sampleValue: f.currentValue, positionNotes: f.extractionQuality,\n   firstSeenBatchId: batchId }))\n        - Also include fields from all tabSections (flattened, appended after\n  header fields, sequential numbering continues)\n    - buttons ← screen.buttons.map(b => ({ text: b.label, position: b.position,\n  apparentFunction: '', firstSeenBatchId: batchId }))\n    - grids ← map each P1Grid to ScreenGrid: { description: grid.name, columns:\n  grid.columns.map(c => ({ header: c.header, type: c.type, sampleValues:\n  c.sampleValues.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), notes:\n  c.extractionQuality })), rowCount: grid.visibleRows, firstSeenBatchId: batchId\n   }\n    - relationships ← [] (A1 doesn't detect relationships)\n    - observations ← screen.observations\n  - renderScreenCatalog(screens: AssembledScreen[], dayNumber: number,\n  sourceFilenames: string[]): string — Render to architecture spec §Output File\n  1 format. Output structure:\n\n  # Day{N} Screen Catalog\n\n  Generated by project-discovery\n  Date: {ISO date}\n  Source: {comma-separated list of sourceFilenames}\n  Screens detected: {count}\n\n  ---\n\n  ## Screen {N}: {Title} ({Form Name})\n\n  **Source:** {source}\n  **Navigation Path:** {path or \"Not determinable from screenshot\"}\n  **Parent Form:** {only if parentForm is set}\n  **Possible Duplicate Of:** {only if possibleDuplicateOf is set}\n\n  ### Header Fields\n\n  | # | Field Label | Type | Current Value | Extraction Quality |\n  |---|-------------|------|---------------|-------------------|\n  | 1 | {label} | {type} | {value} | {quality} |\n\n  ### Grid: {name}\n\n  | # | Column Header | Type | Sample Values | Extraction Quality |\n  |---|--------------|------|---------------|-------------------|\n  | 1 | {header} | {type} | {values} | {quality} |\n\n  **Visible Rows:** {count}\n  **Scroll Indicator:** {Yes/No}\n\n  ### Tabs\n\n  **Active Tab:** {label}\n  **Other Tabs Visible:** {comma-separated}\n\n  #### Tab: {Label}\n\n  | # | Field Label | Type | Current Value | Extraction Quality |\n  |---|-------------|------|---------------|-------------------|\n\n  ### Buttons & Actions\n\n  | # | Button Label | Position | Extraction Quality |\n  |---|-------------|----------|-------------------|\n  | 1 | {label} | {position} | {quality} |\n\n  ### Observations\n\n  - {bullet}\n\n  - Omit sections that have no content (no grids → skip grid section, no tabs →\n  skip tabs section, no parentForm → skip that metadata line).\n  - assembleScreenCatalog(p1Outputs: string[], dayNumber: number,\n  sourceFilenames: string[]): Promise<string> — Main orchestrator:\n    a. Parse all P1 outputs via parseP1Outputs(p1Outputs).\n    b. Separate dialog entries (those with parentForm set) from non-dialog\n  entries.\n    c. For each dialog entry: call splitDialogEntry() → produces two\n  AssembledScreens.\n    d. For non-dialog entries: call groupByTitleBar().\n    e. For each group with >1 entry: call mergeTabEntries() → one\n  AssembledScreen.\n    f. For single-entry groups: convert directly to AssembledScreen.\n    g. Collect all AssembledScreens (from merges, dialog splits, singles).\n    h. Handle unreadable title bars: for entries with [UNCERTAIN] in their title\n   or with possibleDuplicateOf set, check field overlap against all other\n  entries:\n        - > 0.6 → merge (call mergeTabEntries on the pair)\n      - < 0.4 → keep separate\n      - 0.4 - 0.6 → call resolveAmbiguousDedup() — merge if true, keep if false\n    i. Assign sequential numbering: renumber all entries 1, 2, 3... gap-free.\n    j. Call renderScreenCatalog() → return the markdown string.\n\n  Step 6. Create src/lib/pipeline/screen-assembler.test.ts:\n\n  Mock generateText for the Gemini dedup fallback. Fields explicitly\n   attributed to the underlying form → underlying form entry.\n  - Fallback (no clear attribution in observations): fields with [CLEAR]\n  extraction quality → dialog (visible, on top). Fields with [PARTIAL] →\n  underlying form (obscured). Fields with other flags → dialog.\n  - Add disclaimer observation to underlying form: \"Field attribution between\n  dialog and underlying form was inferred from extraction quality flags. Manual\n  review recommended.\"\n  - Dialog entry gets parentForm = entry.parentForm. Underlying form entry gets\n  parentForm = null and screenTitle = entry.parentForm.\n\n  d. calculateFieldOverlap(fieldsA, fieldsB): Normalize labels (lowercase,\n  trim). Otter records audio on a phone — different device, different start time. There is typically ONE Otter transcript per day covering ALL video chunks (3-6 chunks). The offset between video time and Otter time must be calculated per-chunk.\n\n**Proven result:** For Day 1 video, the offset is ~56 seconds (Otter started ~56s before video). Convention: `otterTime = videoTime + offsetSeconds`. Offset is positive when Otter recording started before video.\n\n**Frame extraction:** ffmpeg extracts frames using scene detection (`gt(scene,0.15)`) + interval capture (every 30s). These raw frames include software screens, faces, transitions, blanks. Only software screens are useful for P1 extraction.\n\n## Test Data Paths\n\n- Video: `/Users/jasonburks/Downloads/GMT20260316-191615_Recording_1920x1080 (1).mp4` (91 min, muted mic)\n- Otter transcript: `/Users/jasonburks/Documents/_AI_/TEMPORARY-tap-discovery-compare/TAP-Pipeline/04-discovery-outputs/day1/day1-inputs/TAP Contracts.txt`\n- Artifacts: `/Users/jasonburks/Documents/_AI_/TEMPORARY-tap-discovery-compare/TAP-Pipeline/04-discovery-outputs/day1/day1-inputs/Artifacts/` (Artifact-1.jpeg through Artifact-4.jpeg)\n\nUse these paths in integration test comments, but **do not require them at runtime for unit tests**.
