What the Golden Inputs Do NOT Give You\n\nThe Golden Inputs are extraction-level output. They document what was observed, discussed, captured, and cross-referenced. They are not:\n\n- **Decomposed into concepts/epics/stories** -- That's your pipeline's job. The raw material is there (screens, artifacts, business rules, stakeholder statements) but the decomposition into requirements hierarchy hasn't happened.\n- **Prioritized** -- Business rules are sourced and attributed but not ranked. Some are CEO mandates, some are operator preferences, some are system constraints. Your pipeline needs to assess priority.\n- **Resolved where stakeholders disagree** -- The Golden Inputs document contradictions and design evolutions (e.g., \"one DB with location IDs\" from Day 2 vs \"3 databases\" from Tim's SRD). They flag these, they don't resolve them. Resolution is a requirements-level decision.\n- **Structured for SRD vs PRD split** -- The Tim SRD extraction covers technical approach. The day-level catalogs cover functional needs. But the PRD/SRD boundary (what vs how) hasn't been drawn through the data. Your pipeline draws that line.\n- **Complete on their own** -- The Golden Inputs capture what happened in 3 days of discovery. There are known gaps: Reports submenu never opened, Management category unexplored, Gadsden facility not visited. The Requirements Doc needs to acknowledge these gaps, not paper over them.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What Project-Discovery Is Planning (High Level)\n\nWe're rebuilding our pipeline to take the same raw inputs (Zoom MP4s, Otter transcripts, artifact photos) and produce output comparable to the Golden Inputs. Push-button, repeatable.\n\n**Key things we learned that inform the rebuild:**\n\n- ~50% of sessions have no screenshots (transcript-only). The pipeline must handle this.\n- Business rule extraction is a first-class output, not a byproduct. Day 3 alone had 133.\n- Quality passes (cross-session, cross-day) catch things single-pass extraction misses: forward references, design evolutions, stakeholder threading, hidden confirmations.\n- The process gets richer as it goes -- each session benefits from everything extracted before it (growing corpus effect).\n- Cross-day enrichment is bidirectional: Day 3 findings enrich Day 1 entries, and vice versa.\n\n**We are not building yet.** We're reviewing the plan, identifying gaps (14 found so far), and incorporating operator feedback before any code changes.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The Two-Mode Vision\n\nThis isn't something to build for now. But it should inform how you evaluate your tooling during the audit.\n\n**Mode 1 -- During Discovery (day-by-day):**\n- Project-discovery processes each day's inputs that evening\n- Produces a \"slightly less golden\" day-level extraction (no full QP, no cross-day backward pass)\n- Hands that extraction to tap-discovery's pipeline\n- Tap-discovery produces intermediate outputs: Daily Brief, Facilitator's Guide, gap analysis\n- These outputs shape the next day's facilitation (what to probe deeper, what was missed, what needs clarification)\n- Repeat each night of the engagement\n\n**Mode 2 -- Post-Discovery (back at HQ):**\n- All days available. Project-discovery runs full extraction with cross-session QP, backward pass, enrichment detection\n- Produces Golden Inputs\n- Tap-discovery produces the Requirements Document from Golden Inputs\n\n**Why this matters for your audit:** Some of your existing tooling (Daily Briefs, Facilitator's Guides, gap analysis) may be exactly what Mode 1 needs. Don't throw it out just because the immediate mission is Mode 2 (Requirements Doc). Evaluate it against both modes.\n\n---\n\n## 7. What This Means for Your Audit\n\n1. **Lead with the Requirements Doc mission.** Evaluate every tool against: does this help me produce the Requirements Document from the Golden Inputs? If yes, keep it. If no, set it aside -- don't delete it.\n\n2. **Understand the gap between Golden Inputs and Requirements Doc.** The Golden Inputs give you extracted, cross-referenced, quality-checked discovery data. The Requirements Doc needs decomposed, prioritized, structured requirements. That gap is your pipeline's core job.\n\n3. **Don't rebuild what project-discovery will provide.** We're handling: raw input processing, session extraction, screen/artifact cataloging, business rule extraction, cross-session QP, cross-day enrichment. If your tooling duplicates this, note it as \"covered by upstream\" rather than \"needs rebuilding.\"\n\n4. **Do flag what you need from us that the Golden Inputs don't provide.** If the Requirements Doc process reveals that you need something structured differently, or additional data we didn't extract, or a different format -- that's valuable feedback for our rebuild.\n\n5. **Preserve Mode 1 tooling.** Anything that produces intermediate deliverables (briefs, guides, facilitation support) has a future even if it's not needed for the Requirements Doc. Tag it, don't trash it.\n\n6. **Stay client-agnostic, day-agnostic, project-agnostic.** This discovery was 3 days with TAP. The next might be 2 days remote with a different client. Neither project should hardcode engagement-specific assumptions.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Format, structure, what's guaranteed, what's optional.\n3. **Coordinated rebuild** -- Both projects rebuild their pipelines with shared understanding. No overlap, no gaps, no cross-contamination.\n\nNone of this happens until the Requirements Doc ships. Focus on the deliverable.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Ground Rules for Cross-Project Work\n\nThese protect both projects from the kind of confusion that cost us 3 days when a PDF assumption propagated unchecked:\n\n- **No cross-writing.** Project-discovery does not write to tap-discovery's directories (except at explicit Phase 5 handoff). Not a boundary spec. Not a rebuild plan. Just enough shared understanding to keep both projects aligned while each does its immediate work.\n\n**Date:** April 1, 2026\n\n---\n\n## 1. Your Mission Right Now\n\nProduce the Requirements Document for the client. That's the golden output. Everything else -- audit, tooling, pipeline revamp -- serves that goal or comes after it.\n\nThe Golden Inputs (10 files) are delivered and ready to consume. The Requirements Document prompt defines what the output looks like. Your job is to take those inputs and produce that output at a level most companies couldn't dream of.\n\n**Do not rearchitect your pipeline to produce the Requirements Doc.** Use what you have, fill gaps manually where needed, and learn what the process actually requires by doing it. The tooling rebuild comes after the deliverable ships -- not before, not during.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Both Projects Follow the Same Arc\n\n| | Project-Discovery | Tap-Discovery |\n|--|---|---|\n| **Step 1** | Do the work manually to produce golden output | Do the work manually to produce golden output |\n| **Step 2** | Then build tooling to repeat it | Then build tooling to repeat it |\n| **Golden output** | Golden Inputs (10 files) -- DONE | Requirements Document -- IN PROGRESS |\n| **Rebuild starts** | After Golden Inputs proven | After Requirements Doc ships |\n\nProject-discovery didn't plan its pipeline rebuild until after all 3 days of extraction plus full quality passes were done by hand. That manual process revealed what the pipeline actually needs to do -- things we never would have designed for upfront (transcript-only sessions, 133 business rules in a single day, design evolutions across sessions, artifact re-examination patterns). The same will be true for you: the process of manually producing the Requirements Doc will reveal what your pipeline needs that you can't see yet.\n\n---\n\n## 3. What the Golden Inputs Give You\n\nEach day's output follows the Output Architecture spec (with 14 agreed corrections):\n\n- **Screen Catalog** -- PART 1 (new screens) + PART 2 (cross-day enrichments). Field-level extraction with quality flags. Navigation paths. Dialog-over-form relationships. Tab merges.\n- **Artifact Catalog** -- Sequential global numbering. Field extraction. Document set linking. Cross-day enrichments where artifacts reappear.\n- **Processing Summary** -- Classification table, extraction results, quality flags, cross-session validation, downstream notes, quality pass results with enrichments and corrections.\n- **Tim SRD Extraction** -- Post-discovery technical interview. 21 SRD requirements. Tech stack decisions. Architecture evolution documentation.\n\n**Business rules** are embedded in Processing Summaries (Day 3: 133 BRs with IDs, sources, speakers) and in session narratives referenced by the summaries.\n\n**Cross-day enrichments** connect findings across all 3 days. Day 1 has 25 enrichments linking forward to Days 2-3 findings. Day 2 has 32. Day 3 has 19. These are the connective tissue.\n\n---\n\n## 4. What the Golden Inputs Do NOT Give You\n\nThe Golden Inputs are extraction-level output. They document what was observed, discussed, captured, and cross-referenced. They are not:\n\n- **Decomposed into concepts/epics/stories** -- That's your pipeline's job. The raw material is there (screens, artifacts, business rules, stakeholder statements) but the decomposition into requirements hierarchy hasn't happened.\n- **Prioritized** -- Business rules are sourced and attributed but not ranked. Some are CEO mandates, some are operator preferences, some are system constraints. Your pipeline needs to assess priority.\n- **Resolved where stakeholders disagree** -- The Golden Inputs document contradictions and design evolutions (e.g., \"one DB with location IDs\" from Day 2 vs \"3 databases\" from Tim's SRD). They flag these, they don't resolve them. Resolution is a requirements-level decision.\n- **Structured for SRD vs PRD split** -- The Tim SRD extraction covers technical approach. The day-level catalogs cover functional needs. But the PRD/SRD boundary (what vs how) hasn't been drawn through the data. Your pipeline draws that line.\n- **Complete on their own** -- The Golden Inputs capture what happened in 3 days of discovery. There are known gaps: Reports submenu never opened, Management category unexplored, Gadsden facility not visited. The Requirements Doc needs to acknowledge these gaps, not paper over them.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What Project-Discovery Is Planning (High Level)\n\nWe're rebuilding our pipeline to take the same raw inputs (Zoom MP4s, Otter transcripts, artifact photos) and produce output comparable to the Golden Inputs. Push-button, repeatable.\n\n**Key things we learned that inform the rebuild:**\n\n- ~50% of sessions have no screenshots (transcript-only). The pipeline must handle this.\n- Business rule extraction is a first-class output, not a byproduct. Day 3 alone had 133.\n- Quality passes (cross-session, cross-day) catch things single-pass extraction misses: forward references, design evolutions, stakeholder threading, hidden confirmations.\n- The process gets richer as it goes -- each session benefits from everything extracted before it (growing corpus effect).\n- Cross-day enrichment is bidirectional: Day 3 findings enrich Day 1 entries, and vice versa.\n\n**We are not building yet.** We're reviewing the plan, identifying gaps (14 found so far), and incorporating operator feedback before any code changes.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The Two-Mode Vision\n\nThis isn't something to build for now. But it should inform how you evaluate your tooling during the audit.\n\n**Mode 1 -- During Discovery (day-by-day):**\n- Project-discovery processes each day's inputs that evening\n- Produces a \"slightly less golden\" day-level extraction (no full QP, no cross-day backward pass)\n- Hands that extraction to tap-discovery's pipeline\n- Tap-discovery produces intermediate outputs: Daily Brief, Facilitator's Guide, gap analysis\n- These outputs shape the next day's facilitation (what to probe deeper, what was missed, what needs clarification)\n- Repeat each night of the engagement\n\n**Mode 2 -- Post-Discovery (back at HQ):**\n- All days available. Project-discovery runs full extraction with cross-session QP, backward pass, enrichment detection\n- Produces Golden Inputs\n- Tap-discovery produces the Requirements Document from Golden Inputs\n\n**Why this matters for your audit:** Some of your existing tooling (Daily Briefs, Facilitator's Guides, gap analysis) may be exactly what Mode 1 needs. Don't throw it out just because the immediate mission is Mode 2 (Requirements Doc). Evaluate it against both modes.\n\n---\n\n## 7. What This Means for Your Audit\n\n1. **Lead with the Requirements Doc mission.** Evaluate every tool against: does this help me produce the Requirements Document from the Golden Inputs? If yes, keep it. If no, set it aside -- don't delete it.\n\n2. **Understand the gap between Golden Inputs and Requirements Doc.** The Golden Inputs give you extracted, cross-referenced, quality-checked discovery data. The Requirements Doc needs decomposed, prioritized, structured requirements. That gap is your pipeline's core job.\n\n3. **Don't rebuild what project-discovery will provide.** We're handling: raw input processing, session extraction, screen/artifact cataloging, business rule extraction, cross-session QP, cross-day enrichment. If your tooling duplicates this, note it as \"covered by upstream\" rather than \"needs rebuilding.\"\n\n4. **Do flag what you need from us that the Golden Inputs don't provide.** If the Requirements Doc process reveals that you need something structured differently, or additional data we didn't extract, or a different format -- that's valuable feedback for our rebuild.\n\n5. **Preserve Mode 1 tooling.** Anything that produces intermediate deliverables (briefs, guides, facilitation support) has a future even if it's not needed for the Requirements Doc. Tag it, don't trash it.\n\n6. **Stay client-agnostic, day-agnostic, project-agnostic.** This discovery was 3 days with TAP. The next might be 2 days remote with a different client. Neither project should hardcode engagement-specific assumptions.\n\n---\n\n## 8. What's Coming Next (After Both Golden Outputs Exist)\n\nOnce the Requirements Doc is delivered and project-discovery's pipeline rebuild plan is finalized:\n\n1. **Shared vision doc** -- How both projects fit together. What each side owns. Where the handoff happens. How Mode 1 and Mode 2 work end-to-end.\n2. **Boundary spec** -- Formal interface contract between project-discovery output and tap-discovery input. Format, structure, what's guaranteed, what's optional.\n3. **Coordinated rebuild** -- Both projects rebuild their pipelines with shared understanding. No overlap, no gaps, no cross-contamination.\n\nNone of this happens until the Requirements Doc ships. Focus on the deliverable.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Ground Rules for Cross-Project Work\n\nThese protect both projects from the kind of confusion that cost us 3 days when a PDF assumption propagated unchecked:\n\n- **No cross-writing.** Project-discovery does not write to tap-discovery's directories (except at explicit Phase 5 handoff). Tap-discovery does not write to project-discovery's directories.\n- **No shared assumptions without documentation.** If one project assumes something about the other's output format, behavior, or timeline, it goes in a shared doc -- not in a memory file, not in a brain doc, not in a conversation.\n- **Feedback flows through the operator.** If tap-discovery needs something different from project-discovery (or vice versa), that request goes through the operator, not directly between projects. This prevents context pollution.\n- **Each project owns its own context.** Brain docs, memory files, and CLAUDE.md stay within their project. Use one backend as the system of record.\n2. Keep the memory substrate and Task OS in the same Postgres system.\n3. Do not introduce a second source of truth unless there is an exceptional, explicit decision.\n4. Do not use Notion as the core system of record.\n5. Treat prompts as a behavior layer, not a durable state layer.\n6. Treat structured execution objects as first-class where state matters.\n\n## Product reasoning rules\n\n1. New materials do not automatically change architecture.\n2. Evaluate every new idea against the current baseline.\n3. Prefer additive memos over silent drift.\n4. Name open questions explicitly.\n5. Preserve the distinction between substrate decisions and later interface decisions.\n\n## Retrieval and memory rules\n\n1. One stored item should represent one retrievable thing.\n2. Retrieval scopes matter more than one giant flat pool.\n3. Metadata should stay lightweight and support filtering, routing, and review.\n4. Embeddings do the main retrieval work.\n5. Long-form content should be chunked into meaningful sections before embedding.\n\n## Execution rules\n\n1. Tasks, projects, decisions, and waiting-ons should not be buried as vague metadata inside generic thoughts.\n2. Daily Brief is the first execution surface.\n3. Weekly Review should synthesize both memory and execution objects later, but the first implementation should stay lightweight.\n4. Trust requires receipts, review queues, and visible failures.\n\n## Frontend design rules\n\n1. Visual direction: light and airy with depth. Layered white/off-white surfaces with soft shadows. Dark accents are small and sparse (icon, badge, single element), not entire panels or surfaces.\n2. Stitch reference HTML files are structural references (layout, component shapes, spacing). Not color references. The finalized color direction is light base with modern dark accents, not dark theme.\n3. Token aliasing: ob- prefix dropped from ~30 design tokens. Four tokens keep ob- prefix due to ShadCN/Tailwind collisions: --color-ob-background, --color-ob-primary, --color-ob-emerald-400, --color-ob-emerald-500.\n4. Legibility over aesthetics. If text is hard to read, fix contrast and sizing first. No italic at small sizes. Minimum text-sm (14px) for body content, text-xs (12px) for metadata.\n5. Build the component, screenshot it, then tune. Batch tuning into dedicated passes rather than interrupting builds.\n6. When overlays or panels change the spatial context, tune the base view and overlay together, not separately.\n7. Intricate logos don't read at sidebar scale. Use simple text marks for nav chrome, save detailed logos for larger display contexts.\n8. Route group restructure requires stripping page-level wrappers (min-h-screen, outer main) when the shell layout provides them. Call this out explicitly in build prompts.\n9. Two-column layout with mixed card density creates better visual hierarchy than uniform single-column card stacking. Vary card size and padding by information priority.\n10. System-level status (health, uptime, service state) belongs in persistent chrome (sidebar), not in dashboard cards. It is infrastructure, not mission content.\n11. Prep nudges and secondary metadata render inline with their parent item, not as sub-lines. Sub-lines waste vertical space and disconnect context.\n12. Collision/overload indicators use left border accents, not background tints. Background tints reduce readability of all content in the affected row.\n13. At-distance readability requires vivid hex colors (#22c55e, #f59e0b, #ef4444) at w-2.5+ size, not muted theme tokens. Any status indicator readable at arm's length from a laptop.\n14. Each page owns its header identity via shared PageHeader component with live date. Generic header bar returns null for authenticated pages.\n15. Mock data consolidated in one file per feature area, not scattered per component. Single source of truth for design-time data.\n16. Review Queue earns top-right position on Mission Control. It is the highest-value unique element — surfacing what needs human attention from ingestion.\n17. When two cards show the same domain, merge into one card with summary layer (e.g., segmented bar) and detail layer (e.g., contact list). Do not duplicate domain coverage across cards.\n18. Projects display as card grids (2-column) at 4+ projects, stacked lists for 3 or fewer. Grid scales better for scanning multiple items.\n19. Summary visualizations that double as interaction controls are a preferred pattern. A segmented bar that also filters a table compresses two UI elements into one and teaches the user the data shape through interaction.\n20. Container card pattern: when a group of items needs a \"view all\" link, wrap in a container card (rounded-2xl, shadow-md) with CTA footer. Inner items get lighter backgrounds (bg-surface-container-low/60) for visual layering.\n21. Toast undo that reopens a form must preserve the full form state (not just the text). Lift state management to the component that owns both the toast trigger and the target form. The form passes state up via onConfirm; the parent stores it for undo.\n22. Collapsed sidebar indicators need a dot + 2-letter abbreviation minimum per item. Single icons or dots alone are too ambiguous at w-16 collapsed width.\n23. Never nest `<button>` inside `<button>`. This causes hydration errors in Next.js. Use `<div role=\"button\" tabIndex={0}>` for outer interactive containers that need inner clickable elements.\n24. Multi-item review decisions should be independent, not all-or-nothing. Each item gets its own verdict (merge/different, approve/reject), and the user submits once all decisions are made. Single-action-closes-panel is wrong for multi-step review.\n25. Two-phase flows (triage → confirmation) are more intuitive than cramming everything into one screen for complex decisions. Triage = make choices. Confirmation = review summary + edit + approve.\n26. AI classification decisions (type, project, contact) should populate from AI's proposed_action text parsing, not just explicit candidates. The proposed_action string is a structured sentence — parse it to extract project names, contact names, and item types.\n27. Workflow interruption needs recovery. If a user accidentally closes a mid-workflow panel, provide a \"Resume\" entry point in the originating UI. Track pending state separately from active state.\n28. \"Reference\" is a distinct type from \"Note\". Reference = external content bookmarked for retrieval (articles, links, saved resources). Note = user-authored observations, thoughts, memos. Article/link captures should default to Reference classification.\n29. AI prompt/insight logic lives in dedicated config files (lib/ai-prompts.ts), not inline in components. Each prompt entry documents which component and location uses it. This keeps AI behavior auditable as the system grows across surfaces.\n30. Save/Cancel for edit modes uses a pinned bottom bar in the same position as the primary action bar (Mark Complete/Snooze/Delete). The action bar and edit bar are mutually exclusive — show one or the other based on editing state. Do not put Save/Cancel in the panel header.\n31. Multi-entity relationships (task → multiple projects, task → multiple contacts) use the add/remove chip pattern: existing items as removable pills, plus an \"Add [entity]\" dashed-border button that opens a picker dropdown. Filter already-selected items from the picker list.\n\n## Simplicity rules\n\n1. Prefer the simplest design that preserves portability, trust, and future extensibility.\n2. Reject complexity that does not clearly improve reliability, review quality, retrieval quality, or operator leverage.\n3. Delay frontend-heavy work until the backend loop proves itself.\n4. Delay high-sensitivity ingestion, such as email, until scopes and trust rules are stable.\n\n## Development-method rules\n\n1. Foundation Doc before PRD when architecture, vocabulary, contracts, or phase boundaries are still being decided.\n2. PRD before Spec-Kit execution.\n3. Constitution before implementation.\n4. Human review between every major spec-driven step.\n5. Keep canonical decisions in files, not only in chat.\n6. Gates are not optional. If a gate is defined in the build sequence, it must be completed and its findings reviewed before any work past that gate begins. Code built ahead of a gate is provisional until the gate passes.\n7. Separate exploration sessions from build sessions. If the operator is exploring, do not force output. If building, ship something. Do not let an exploration session accidentally become a build session.\n\n## What to optimize for\n\n- portability\n- reliability\n- operator clarity\n- future-proof contracts\n- non-technical explainability\n- practical buildability\n\n## Context management rules\n\n1. Do not treat mounted project files or chat-attached files as source of truth. The repo is the source of truth.\n2. When expanding context, request files by name and path from the repo. Do not work from memory or stale uploads.\n3. The central brain (this Claude project) reasons about the product. It does not store canonical files. Canonical files live in the repo and in the brain docs at the project root.\n\n## Claude Code working rules\n\n1. Read brain-RULES.md and brain-SESSION-START.md at the start of every session.\n2. Use one backend as the system of record.\n2. Keep the memory substrate and Task OS in the same Postgres system.\n3. Do not introduce a second source of truth unless there is an exceptional, explicit decision.\n4. Do not use Notion as the core system of record.\n5. Retrieval scopes matter more than one giant flat pool.\n3. Metadata should stay lightweight and support filtering, routing, and review.\n4. Embeddings do the main retrieval work.\n5. Long-form content should be chunked into meaningful sections before embedding.\n\n## Execution rules\n1. Tasks, projects, decisions, and waiting-ons should not be buried as vague metadata inside generic thoughts.\n2. Daily Brief is the first execution surface.\n3. Weekly Review should synthesize both memory and execution objects later, but the first implementation should stay lightweight.\n4. Trust requires receipts, review queues, and visible failures.\n\n## Frontend design rules\n1. Visual direction: light and airy with depth. Layered white/off-white surfaces with soft shadows. Dark accents are small and sparse (icon, badge, single element), not entire panels or surfaces.\n2. Stitch reference HTML files are structural references (layout, component shapes, spacing). Not color references. The finalized color direction is light base with modern dark accents, not dark theme.\n3. Token aliasing: ob- prefix dropped from ~30 design tokens. Four tokens keep ob- prefix due to ShadCN/Tailwind collisions: --color-ob-background, --color-ob-primary, --color-ob-emerald-400, --color-ob-emerald-500.\n4. Legibility over aesthetics. If text is hard to read, fix contrast and sizing first. No italic at small sizes. Minimum text-sm (14px) for body content, text-xs (12px) for metadata.\n5. Build the component, screenshot it, then tune. Batch tuning into dedicated passes rather than interrupting builds.\n6. When overlays or panels change the spatial context, tune the base view and overlay together, not separately.\n7. Intricate logos don't read at sidebar scale. Use simple text marks for nav chrome, save detailed logos for larger display contexts.\n8. Route group restructure requires stripping page-level wrappers (min-h-screen, outer main) when the shell layout provides them. Call this out explicitly in build prompts.\n9. Two-column layout with mixed card density creates better visual hierarchy than uniform single-column card stacking. Vary card size and padding by information priority.\n\n## Simplicity rules\n1. Prefer the simplest design that preserves portability, trust, and future extensibility.\n2. Reject complexity that does not clearly improve reliability, review quality, retrieval quality, or operator leverage.\n3. Delay frontend-heavy work until the backend loop proves itself.\n4. Delay high-sensitivity ingestion, such as email, until scopes and trust rules are stable.\n\n## Development-method rules\n1. Foundation Doc before PRD when architecture, vocabulary, contracts, or phase boundaries are still being decided.\n2. PRD before Spec-Kit execution.\n3. Constitution before implementation.\n4. Human review between every major spec-driven step.\n5. Keep canonical decisions in files, not only in chat.\n6. Gates are not optional. If a gate is defined in the build sequence, it must be completed and its findings reviewed before any work past that gate begins. Code built ahead of a gate is provisional until the gate passes.\n7. Separate exploration sessions from build sessions. If the operator is exploring, do not force output. If building, ship something. Do not let an exploration session accidentally become a build session.\n\n## What to optimize for\n- portability\n- reliability\n- operator clarity\n- future-proof contracts\n- non-technical explainability\n- practical buildability\n\n## Context management rules\n1. Do not treat mounted project files or chat-attached files as source of truth. The repo is the source of truth.\n2. When expanding context, request files by name and path from the repo. Do not work from memory or stale uploads.\n3. The central brain (this Claude project) reasons about the product. It does not store canonical files. If text is hard to read, fix contrast and sizing first. No italic at small sizes. Minimum text-sm (14px) for body content, text-xs (12px) for metadata.\n    36→5. Build the component, screenshot it, then tune. Batch tuning into dedicated passes rather than interrupting builds.\n    37→6. Tasks, projects, decisions, and waiting-ons should not be buried as vague metadata inside generic thoughts.\n2. Daily Brief is the first execution surface.\n3. Weekly Review should synthesize both memory and execution objects later, but the first implementation should stay lightweight.\n4. Trust requires receipts, review queues, and visible failures.\n\n## Frontend design rules\n1. Visual direction: light and airy with depth. Layered white/off-white surfaces with soft shadows. Dark accents are small and sparse (icon, badge, single element), not entire panels or surfaces.\n2. Stitch reference HTML files are structural references (layout, component shapes, spacing). Not color references. The finalized color direction is light base with modern dark accents, not dark theme.\n3. Token aliasing: ob- prefix dropped from ~30 design tokens. Single-action-closes-panel is wrong for multi-step review.\n25. Two-phase flows (triage → confirmation) are more intuitive than cramming everything into one screen for complex decisions. Triage = make choices. Confirmation = review summary + edit + approve.\n26. Note = user-authored observations, thoughts, memos. Article/link captures should default to Reference classification.\n29. AI prompt/insight logic lives in dedicated config files (lib/ai-prompts.ts), not inline in components. Each prompt entry documents which component and location uses it. This keeps AI behavior auditable as the system grows across surfaces.\n30. The action bar and edit bar are mutually exclusive — show one or the other based on editing state. Do not put Save/Cancel in the panel header.\n31. Use one backend as the system of record.\n2. Keep the memory substrate and Task OS in the same Postgres system.\n3. Do not introduce a second source of truth unless there is an exceptional, explicit decision.\n4. Do not use Notion as the core system of record.\n5. New materials do not automatically change architecture.\n2. Evaluate every new idea against the current baseline.\n3. Prefer additive memos over silent drift.\n4. Name open questions explicitly.\n5. Preserve the distinction between substrate decisions and later interface decisions.\n\n## Retrieval and memory rules\n\n1. One stored item should represent one retrievable thing.\n2. Retrieval scopes matter more than one giant flat pool.\n3. Metadata should stay lightweight and support filtering, routing, and review.\n4. Embeddings do the main retrieval work.\n5. Long-form content should be chunked into meaningful sections before embedding.\n\n## Execution rules\n\n1. Tasks, projects, decisions, and waiting-ons should not be buried as vague metadata inside generic thoughts.\n2. Daily Brief is the first execution surface.\n3. Weekly Review should synthesize both memory and execution objects later, but the first implementation should stay lightweight.\n4. Trust requires receipts, review queues, and visible failures.\n\n## Frontend design rules\n\n1. Visual direction: light and airy with depth. Layered white/off-white surfaces with soft shadows. Dark accents are small and sparse (icon, badge, single element), not entire panels or surfaces.\n2. Stitch reference HTML files are structural references (layout, component shapes, spacing). Not color references. The finalized color direction is light base with modern dark accents, not dark theme.\n3. Token aliasing: ob- prefix dropped from ~30 design tokens. Four tokens keep ob- prefix due to ShadCN/Tailwind collisions: --color-ob-background, --color-ob-primary, --color-ob-emerald-400, --color-ob-emerald-500.\n4. Legibility over aesthetics. If text is hard to read, fix contrast and sizing first. No italic at small sizes. Minimum text-sm (14px) for body content, text-xs (12px) for metadata.\n5. Build the component, screenshot it, then tune. Batch tuning into dedicated passes rather than interrupting builds.\n6. When overlays or panels change the spatial context, tune the base view and overlay together, not separately.\n7. Intricate logos don't read at sidebar scale. Use simple text marks for nav chrome, save detailed logos for larger display contexts.\n8. Route group restructure requires stripping page-level wrappers (min-h-screen, outer main) when the shell layout provides them. Call this out explicitly in build prompts.\n9. Two-column layout with mixed card density creates better visual hierarchy than uniform single-column card stacking. Vary card size and padding by information priority.\n10. System-level status (health, uptime, service state) belongs in persistent chrome (sidebar), not in dashboard cards. It is infrastructure, not mission content.\n11. Prep nudges and secondary metadata render inline with their parent item, not as sub-lines. Sub-lines waste vertical space and disconnect context.\n12. A segmented bar that also filters a table compresses two UI elements into one and teaches the user the data shape through interaction.\n20. Plugin marketplaces are catalogs that help you discover and install these extensions without building them yourself.\n\nLooking to create and distribute your own marketplace? See [Create and distribute a plugin marketplace](/en/plugin-marketplaces).\n\n## How marketplaces work\n\nA marketplace is a catalog of plugins that someone else has created and shared. Using a marketplace is a two-step process:\n\n<Steps>\n  <Step title=\"Add the marketplace\">\n    This registers the catalog with Claude Code so you can browse what's available. No plugins are installed yet.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Install individual plugins\">\n    Browse the catalog and install the plugins you want.\n  </Step>\n</Steps>\n\nThink of it like adding an app store: adding the store gives you access to browse its collection, but you still choose which apps to download individually.\n\n## Official Anthropic marketplace\n\nThe official Anthropic marketplace (`claude-plugins-official`) is automatically available when you start Claude Code. Run `/plugin` and go to the **Discover** tab to browse what's available, or view the catalog at [claude.com/plugins](https://claude.com/plugins).\n\nTo install a plugin from the official marketplace, use `/plugin install <name>@claude-plugins-official`. For example, to install the GitHub integration:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin install github@claude-plugins-official\n```\n\nIf Claude Code reports that the plugin is not found in any marketplace, your marketplace is either missing or outdated. Run `/plugin marketplace update claude-plugins-official` to refresh it, or `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official` if you haven't added it before. Then retry the install.\n\n<Note>\n  The official marketplace is maintained by Anthropic. To submit a plugin to the official marketplace, use one of the in-app submission forms:\n\n  * **Claude.ai**: [claude.ai/settings/plugins/submit](https://claude.ai/settings/plugins/submit)\n  * **Console**: [platform.claude.com/plugins/submit](https://platform.claude.com/plugins/submit)\n\n  To distribute plugins independently, [create your own marketplace](/en/plugin-marketplaces) and share it with users.\n</Note>\n\nThe official marketplace includes several categories of plugins:\n\n### Code intelligence\n\nCode intelligence plugins enable Claude Code's built-in LSP tool, giving Claude the ability to jump to definitions, find references, and see type errors immediately after edits. These plugins configure [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) connections, the same technology that powers VS Code's code intelligence.\n\nThese plugins require the language server binary to be installed on your system. If you already have a language server installed, Claude may prompt you to install the corresponding plugin when you open a project.\n\n| Language   | Plugin              | Binary required              |\n| :--------- | :------------------ | :--------------------------- |\n| C/C++      | `clangd-lsp`        | `clangd`                     |\n| C#         | `csharp-lsp`        | `csharp-ls`                  |\n| Go         | `gopls-lsp`         | `gopls`                      |\n| Java       | `jdtls-lsp`         | `jdtls`                      |\n| Kotlin     | `kotlin-lsp`        | `kotlin-language-server`     |\n| Lua        | `lua-lsp`           | `lua-language-server`        |\n| PHP        | `php-lsp`           | `intelephense`               |\n| Python     | `pyright-lsp`       | `pyright-langserver`         |\n| Rust       | `rust-analyzer-lsp` | `rust-analyzer`              |\n| Swift      | `swift-lsp`         | `sourcekit-lsp`              |\n| TypeScript | `typescript-lsp`    | `typescript-language-server` |\n\nYou can also [create your own LSP plugin](/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers) for other languages.\n\n<Note>\n  If you see `Executable not found in $PATH` in the `/plugin` Errors tab after installing a plugin, install the required binary from the table above.\n</Note>\n\n#### What Claude gains from code intelligence plugins\n\nOnce a code intelligence plugin is installed and its language server binary is available, Claude gains two capabilities:\n\n* **Automatic diagnostics**: after every file edit Claude makes, the language server analyzes the changes and reports errors and warnings back automatically. Claude sees type errors, missing imports, and syntax issues without needing to run a compiler or linter. If Claude introduces an error, it notices and fixes the issue in the same turn. This requires no configuration beyond installing the plugin. You can see diagnostics inline by pressing **Ctrl+O** when the \"diagnostics found\" indicator appears.\n* **Code navigation**: Claude can use the language server to jump to definitions, find references, get type info on hover, list symbols, find implementations, and trace call hierarchies. These operations give Claude more precise navigation than grep-based search, though availability may vary by language and environment.\n\nIf you run into issues, see [Code intelligence troubleshooting](#code-intelligence-issues).\n\n### External integrations\n\nThese plugins bundle pre-configured [MCP servers](/en/mcp) so you can connect Claude to external services without manual setup:\n\n* **Source control**: `github`, `gitlab`\n* **Project management**: `atlassian` (Jira/Confluence), `asana`, `linear`, `notion`\n* **Design**: `figma`\n* **Infrastructure**: `vercel`, `firebase`, `supabase`\n* **Communication**: `slack`\n* **Monitoring**: `sentry`\n\n### Development workflows\n\nPlugins that add skills and agents for common development tasks:\n\n* **commit-commands**: Git commit workflows including commit, push, and PR creation\n* **pr-review-toolkit**: Specialized agents for reviewing pull requests\n* **agent-sdk-dev**: Tools for building with the Claude Agent SDK\n* **plugin-dev**: Toolkit for creating your own plugins\n\n### Output styles\n\nCustomize how Claude responds:\n\n* **explanatory-output-style**: Educational insights about implementation choices\n* **learning-output-style**: Interactive learning mode for skill building\n\n## Try it: add the demo marketplace\n\nAnthropic also maintains a [demo plugins marketplace](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins) (`claude-code-plugins`) with example plugins that show what's possible with the plugin system. Unlike the official marketplace, you need to add this one manually.\n\n<Steps>\n  <Step title=\"Add the marketplace\">\n    From within Claude Code, run the `plugin marketplace add` command for the `anthropics/claude-code` marketplace:\n\n    ```shell theme={null}\n    /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-code\n    ```\n\n    This downloads the marketplace catalog and makes its plugins available to you.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Browse available plugins\">\n    Run `/plugin` to open the plugin manager. This opens a tabbed interface with four tabs you can cycle through using **Tab** (or **Shift+Tab** to go backward):\n\n    * **Discover**: browse available plugins from all your marketplaces\n    * **Installed**: view and manage your installed plugins\n    * **Marketplaces**: add, remove, or update your added marketplaces\n    * **Errors**: view any plugin loading errors\n\n    Go to the **Discover** tab to see plugins from the marketplace you just added.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Install a plugin\">\n    Select a plugin to view its details, then choose an installation scope:\n\n    * **User scope**: install for yourself across all projects\n    * **Project scope**: install for all collaborators on this repository\n    * **Local scope**: install for yourself in this repository only\n\n    For example, select **commit-commands** (a plugin that adds git workflow skills) and install it to your user scope.\n\n    You can also install directly from the command line:\n\n    ```shell theme={null}\n    /plugin install commit-commands@anthropics-claude-code\n    ```\n\n    See [Configuration scopes](/en/settings#configuration-scopes) to learn more about scopes.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Use your new plugin\">\n    After installing, run `/reload-plugins` to activate the plugin. Plugin skills are namespaced by the plugin name, so **commit-commands** provides skills like `/commit-commands:commit`.\n\n    Try it out by making a change to a file and running:\n\n    ```shell theme={null}\n    /commit-commands:commit\n    ```\n\n    This stages your changes, generates a commit message, and creates the commit.\n\n    Each plugin works differently. Plugin marketplaces are catalogs that help you discover and install these extensions without building them yourself.\n\nLooking to create and distribute your own marketplace? See [Create and distribute a plugin marketplace](/en/plugin-marketplaces).\n\n## How marketplaces work\n\nA marketplace is a catalog of plugins that someone else has created and shared. Using a marketplace is a two-step process:\n\n<Steps>\n  <Step title=\"Add the marketplace\">\n    This registers the catalog with Claude Code so you can browse what's available. No plugins are installed yet.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Install individual plugins\">\n    Browse the catalog and install the plugins you want.\n  </Step>\n</Steps>\n\nThink of it like adding an app store: adding the store gives you access to browse its collection, but you still choose which apps to download individually.\n\n## Official Anthropic marketplace\n\nThe official Anthropic marketplace (`claude-plugins-official`) is automatically available when you start Claude Code. Run `/plugin` and go to the **Discover** tab to browse what's available, or view the catalog at [claude.com/plugins](https://claude.com/plugins).\n\nTo install a plugin from the official marketplace, use `/plugin install <name>@claude-plugins-official`. For example, to install the GitHub integration:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin install github@claude-plugins-official\n```\n\nIf Claude Code reports that the plugin is not found in any marketplace, your marketplace is either missing or outdated. Run `/plugin marketplace update claude-plugins-official` to refresh it, or `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official` if you haven't added it before. Then retry the install.\n\n<Note>\n  The official marketplace is maintained by Anthropic. To submit a plugin to the official marketplace, use one of the in-app submission forms:\n\n  * **Claude.ai**: [claude.ai/settings/plugins/submit](https://claude.ai/settings/plugins/submit)\n  * **Console**: [platform.claude.com/plugins/submit](https://platform.claude.com/plugins/submit)\n\n  To distribute plugins independently, [create your own marketplace](/en/plugin-marketplaces) and share it with users.\n</Note>\n\nThe official marketplace includes several categories of plugins:\n\n### Code intelligence\n\nCode intelligence plugins enable Claude Code's built-in LSP tool, giving Claude the ability to jump to definitions, find references, and see type errors immediately after edits. These plugins configure [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) connections, the same technology that powers VS Code's code intelligence.\n\nThese plugins require the language server binary to be installed on your system. If you already have a language server installed, Claude may prompt you to install the corresponding plugin when you open a project.\n\n| Language   | Plugin              | Binary required              |\n| :--------- | :------------------ | :--------------------------- |\n| C/C++      | `clangd-lsp`        | `clangd`                     |\n| C#         | `csharp-lsp`        | `csharp-ls`                  |\n| Go         | `gopls-lsp`         | `gopls`                      |\n| Java       | `jdtls-lsp`         | `jdtls`                      |\n| Kotlin     | `kotlin-lsp`        | `kotlin-language-server`     |\n| Lua        | `lua-lsp`           | `lua-language-server`        |\n| PHP        | `php-lsp`           | `intelephense`               |\n| Python     | `pyright-lsp`       | `pyright-langserver`         |\n| Rust       | `rust-analyzer-lsp` | `rust-analyzer`              |\n| Swift      | `swift-lsp`         | `sourcekit-lsp`              |\n| TypeScript | `typescript-lsp`    | `typescript-language-server` |\n\nYou can also [create your own LSP plugin](/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers) for other languages.\n\n<Note>\n  If you see `Executable not found in $PATH` in the `/plugin` Errors tab after installing a plugin, install the required binary from the table above.\n</Note>\n\n#### What Claude gains from code intelligence plugins\n\nOnce a code intelligence plugin is installed and its language server binary is available, Claude gains two capabilities:\n\n* **Automatic diagnostics**: after every file edit Claude makes, the language server analyzes the changes and reports errors and warnings back automatically. Claude sees type errors, missing imports, and syntax issues without needing to run a compiler or linter. If Claude introduces an error, it notices and fixes the issue in the same turn. This requires no configuration beyond installing the plugin. You can see diagnostics inline by pressing **Ctrl+O** when the \"diagnostics found\" indicator appears.\n* **Code navigation**: Claude can use the language server to jump to definitions, find references, get type info on hover, list symbols, find implementations, and trace call hierarchies. These operations give Claude more precise navigation than grep-based search, though availability may vary by language and environment.\n\nIf you run into issues, see [Code intelligence troubleshooting](#code-intelligence-issues).\n\n### External integrations\n\nThese plugins bundle pre-configured [MCP servers](/en/mcp) so you can connect Claude to external services without manual setup:\n\n* **Source control**: `github`, `gitlab`\n* **Project management**: `atlassian` (Jira/Confluence), `asana`, `linear`, `notion`\n* **Design**: `figma`\n* **Infrastructure**: `vercel`, `firebase`, `supabase`\n* **Communication**: `slack`\n* **Monitoring**: `sentry`\n\n### Development workflows\n\nPlugins that add skills and agents for common development tasks:\n\n* **commit-commands**: Git commit workflows including commit, push, and PR creation\n* **pr-review-toolkit**: Specialized agents for reviewing pull requests\n* **agent-sdk-dev**: Tools for building with the Claude Agent SDK\n* **plugin-dev**: Toolkit for creating your own plugins\n\n### Output styles\n\nCustomize how Claude responds:\n\n* **explanatory-output-style**: Educational insights about implementation choices\n* **learning-output-style**: Interactive learning mode for skill building\n\n## Try it: add the demo marketplace\n\nAnthropic also maintains a [demo plugins marketplace](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins) (`claude-code-plugins`) with example plugins that show what's possible with the plugin system. Unlike the official marketplace, you need to add this one manually.\n\n<Steps>\n  <Step title=\"Add the marketplace\">\n    From within Claude Code, run the `plugin marketplace add` command for the `anthropics/claude-code` marketplace:\n\n    ```shell theme={null}\n    /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-code\n    ```\n\n    This downloads the marketplace catalog and makes its plugins available to you.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Browse available plugins\">\n    Run `/plugin` to open the plugin manager. This opens a tabbed interface with four tabs you can cycle through using **Tab** (or **Shift+Tab** to go backward):\n\n    * **Discover**: browse available plugins from all your marketplaces\n    * **Installed**: view and manage your installed plugins\n    * **Marketplaces**: add, remove, or update your added marketplaces\n    * **Errors**: view any plugin loading errors\n\n    Go to the **Discover** tab to see plugins from the marketplace you just added.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Install a plugin\">\n    Select a plugin to view its details, then choose an installation scope:\n\n    * **User scope**: install for yourself across all projects\n    * **Project scope**: install for all collaborators on this repository\n    * **Local scope**: install for yourself in this repository only\n\n    For example, select **commit-commands** (a plugin that adds git workflow skills) and install it to your user scope.\n\n    You can also install directly from the command line:\n\n    ```shell theme={null}\n    /plugin install commit-commands@anthropics-claude-code\n    ```\n\n    See [Configuration scopes](/en/settings#configuration-scopes) to learn more about scopes.\n  </Step>\n\n  <Step title=\"Use your new plugin\">\n    After installing, run `/reload-plugins` to activate the plugin. Plugin skills are namespaced by the plugin name, so **commit-commands** provides skills like `/commit-commands:commit`.\n\n    Try it out by making a change to a file and running:\n\n    ```shell theme={null}\n    /commit-commands:commit\n    ```\n\n    This stages your changes, generates a commit message, and creates the commit.\n\n    Each plugin works differently. Check the plugin's description in the **Discover** tab or its homepage to learn what skills and capabilities it provides.\n  </Step>\n</Steps>\n\nThe rest of this guide covers all the ways you can add marketplaces, install plugins, and manage your configuration.\n\n## Add marketplaces\n\nUse the `/plugin marketplace add` command to add marketplaces from different sources.\n\n<Tip>\n  **Shortcuts**: You can use `/plugin market` instead of `/plugin marketplace`, and `rm` instead of `remove`.\n</Tip>\n\n* **GitHub repositories**: `owner/repo` format (for example, `anthropics/claude-code`)\n* **Git URLs**: any git repository URL (GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)\n* **Local paths**: directories or direct paths to `marketplace.json` files\n* **Remote URLs**: direct URLs to hosted `marketplace.json` files\n\n### Add from GitHub\n\nAdd a GitHub repository that contains a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file using the `owner/repo` format—where `owner` is the GitHub username or organization and `repo` is the repository name.\n\nFor example, `anthropics/claude-code` refers to the `claude-code` repository owned by `anthropics`:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-code\n```\n\n### Add from other Git hosts\n\nAdd any git repository by providing the full URL. This works with any Git host, including GitLab, Bitbucket, and self-hosted servers:\n\nUsing HTTPS:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.com/company/plugins.git\n```\n\nUsing SSH:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add git@gitlab.com:company/plugins.git\n```\n\nTo add a specific branch or tag, append `#` followed by the ref:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add https://gitlab.com/company/plugins.git#v1.0.0\n```\n\n### Add from local paths\n\nAdd a local directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add ./my-marketplace\n```\n\nYou can also add a direct path to a `marketplace.json` file:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add ./path/to/marketplace.json\n```\n\n### Add from remote URLs\n\nAdd a remote `marketplace.json` file via URL:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace add https://example.com/marketplace.json\n```\n\n<Note>\n  URL-based marketplaces have some limitations compared to Git-based marketplaces. If you encounter \"path not found\" errors when installing plugins, see [Troubleshooting](/en/plugin-marketplaces#plugins-with-relative-paths-fail-in-url-based-marketplaces).\n</Note>\n\n## Install plugins\n\nOnce you've added marketplaces, you can install plugins directly (installs to user scope by default):\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin install plugin-name@marketplace-name\n```\n\nTo choose a different [installation scope](/en/settings#configuration-scopes), use the interactive UI: run `/plugin`, go to the **Discover** tab, and press **Enter** on a plugin. You'll see options for:\n\n* **User scope** (default): install for yourself across all projects\n* **Project scope**: install for all collaborators on this repository (adds to `.claude/settings.json`)\n* **Local scope**: install for yourself in this repository only (not shared with collaborators)\n\nYou may also see plugins with **managed** scope—these are installed by administrators via [managed settings](/en/settings#settings-files) and cannot be modified.\n\n<Warning>\n  Make sure you trust a plugin before installing it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they work as intended. Check each plugin's homepage for more information.\n</Warning>\n\n## Manage installed plugins\n\nRun `/plugin` and go to the **Installed** tab to view, enable, disable, or uninstall your plugins. The list is grouped by scope and sorted so you see problems first: plugins with load errors or unresolved dependencies appear at the top, followed by your favorites, with disabled plugins folded behind a collapsed header at the bottom.\n\nFrom the list you can:\n\n* press `f` to favorite or unfavorite the selected plugin\n* type to filter by plugin name or description\n* press Enter to open a plugin's detail view and enable, disable, or uninstall it\n\nWhen you install a plugin that declares dependencies, the install output lists which dependencies were auto-installed alongside it.\n\nYou can also manage plugins with direct commands.\n\nDisable a plugin without uninstalling:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin disable plugin-name@marketplace-name\n```\n\nRe-enable a disabled plugin:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin enable plugin-name@marketplace-name\n```\n\nCompletely remove a plugin:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin uninstall plugin-name@marketplace-name\n```\n\nThe `--scope` option lets you target a specific scope with CLI commands:\n\n```shell theme={null}\nclaude plugin install formatter@your-org --scope project\nclaude plugin uninstall formatter@your-org --scope project\n```\n\n### Apply plugin changes without restarting\n\nWhen you install, enable, or disable plugins during a session, run `/reload-plugins` to pick up all changes without restarting:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/reload-plugins\n```\n\nClaude Code reloads all active plugins and shows counts for plugins, skills, agents, hooks, plugin MCP servers, and plugin LSP servers.\n\n## Manage marketplaces\n\nYou can manage marketplaces through the interactive `/plugin` interface or with CLI commands.\n\n### Use the interactive interface\n\nRun `/plugin` and go to the **Marketplaces** tab to:\n\n* View all your added marketplaces with their sources and status\n* Add new marketplaces\n* Update marketplace listings to fetch the latest plugins\n* Remove marketplaces you no longer need\n\n### Use CLI commands\n\nYou can also manage marketplaces with direct commands.\n\nList all configured marketplaces:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace list\n```\n\nRefresh plugin listings from a marketplace:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace update marketplace-name\n```\n\nRemove a marketplace:\n\n```shell theme={null}\n/plugin marketplace remove marketplace-name\n```\n\n<Warning>\n  Removing a marketplace will uninstall any plugins you installed from it.\n</Warning>\n\n### Configure auto-updates\n\nClaude Code can automatically update marketplaces and their installed plugins at startup. When auto-update is enabled for a marketplace, Claude Code refreshes the marketplace data and updates installed plugins to their latest versions. If any plugins were updated, you'll see a notification prompting you to run `/reload-plugins`.\n\nToggle auto-update for individual marketplaces through the UI:\n\n1. Run `/plugin` to open the plugin manager\n2. Select **Marketplaces**\n3. Choose a marketplace from the list\n4. Select **Enable auto-update** or **Disable auto-update**\n\nOfficial Anthropic marketplaces have auto-update enabled by default. Third-party and local development marketplaces have auto-update disabled by default.\n\nTo disable all automatic updates entirely for both Claude Code and all plugins, set the `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` environment variable. See [Auto updates](/en/setup#auto-updates) for details.\n\nTo keep plugin auto-updates enabled while disabling Claude Code auto-updates, set `FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS=1` along with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`:\n\n```bash theme={null}\nexport DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1\nexport FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS=1\n```\n\nThis is useful when you want to manage Claude Code updates manually but still receive automatic plugin updates.\n\n## Configure team marketplaces\n\nTeam admins can set up automatic marketplace installation for projects by adding marketplace configuration to `.claude/settings.json`. When team members trust the repository folder, Claude Code prompts them to install these marketplaces and plugins.\n\nAdd `extraKnownMarketplaces` to your project's `.claude/settings.json`:\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"extraKnownMarketplaces\": {\n    \"my-team-tools\": {\n      \"source\": {\n        \"source\": \"github\",\n        \"repo\": \"your-org/claude-plugins\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nFor full configuration options including `extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins`, see [Plugin settings](/en/settings#plugin-settings).\n\n## Security\n\nPlugins and marketplaces are highly trusted components that can execute arbitrary code on your machine with your user privileges. Only install plugins and add marketplaces from sources you trust. Organizations can restrict which marketplaces users are allowed to add using [managed marketplace restrictions](/en/plugin-marketplaces#managed-marketplace-restrictions).\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### /plugin command not recognized\n\nIf you see \"unknown command\" or the `/plugin` command doesn't appear:\n\n1. **Check your version**: Run `claude --version` to see what's installed.\n2. **Update Claude Code**:\n   * **Homebrew**: `brew upgrade claude-code` (or `brew upgrade claude-code@latest` if you installed that cask)\n   * **npm**: `npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`\n   * **Native installer**: Re-run the install command from [Setup](/en/setup)\n3. **Restart Claude Code**: After updating, restart your terminal and run `claude` again.\n\n### Common issues\n\n* **Marketplace not loading**: Verify the URL is accessible and that `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` exists at the path\n* **Plugin installation failures**: Check that plugin source URLs are accessible and repositories are public (or you have access)\n* **Files not found after installation**: Plugins are copied to a cache, so paths referencing files outside the plugin directory won't work\n* **Plugin skills not appearing**: Clear the cache with `rm -rf ~/.claude/plugins/cache`, restart Claude Code, and reinstall the plugin.\n\nFor detailed troubleshooting with solutions, see [Troubleshooting](/en/plugin-marketplaces#troubleshooting) in the marketplace guide. For debugging tools, see [Debugging and development tools](/en/plugins-reference#debugging-and-development-tools).\n\n### Code intelligence issues\n\n* **Language server not starting**: verify the binary is installed and available in your `$PATH`. Check the `/plugin` Errors tab for details.\n* **High memory usage**: language servers like `rust-analyzer` and `pyright` can consume significant memory on large projects. If you experience memory issues, disable the plugin with `/plugin disable <plugin-name>` and rely on Claude's built-in search tools instead.\n* **False positive diagnostics in monorepos**: language servers may report unresolved import errors for internal packages if the workspace isn't configured correctly. These don't affect Claude's ability to edit code.\n\n## Next steps\n\n* **Build your own plugins**: See [Plugins](/en/plugins) to create skills, agents, and hooks\n* **Create a marketplace**: See [Create a plugin marketplace](/en/plugin-marketplaces) to distribute plugins to your team or community\n* **Technical reference**: See [Plugins reference](/en/plugins-reference) for complete specifications\n"}]},"uuid":"f792eb9f-f281-431c-bd3c-46d47f71d49a","timestamp":"2026-04-18T16:00:54.264Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"77fd12b2-b203-405b-b3ae-b3c35a97f8c0","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/jasonburks/Documents/_AI_/Civ | Meeting Notes","sessionId":"22de7eca-40ab-4aa9-baaa-bc35a7f609e6","version":"2.1.92","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"linked-soaring-puddle"}

Your pipeline needs to assess priority.\n- **Resolved where stakeholders disagree** -- The Golden Inputs document contradictions and design evolutions (e.g., \"one DB with location IDs\" from Day 2 vs \"3 databases\" from Tim's SRD). They flag these, they don't resolve them. Resolution is a requirements-level decision.\n- **Structured for SRD vs PRD split** -- The Tim SRD extraction covers technical approach. The day-level catalogs cover functional needs. But the PRD/SRD boundary (what vs how) hasn't been drawn through the data. Your pipeline draws that line.\n- **Complete on their own** -- The Golden Inputs capture what happened in 3 days of discovery. There are known gaps: Reports submenu never opened, Management category unexplored, Gadsden facility not visited. The Requirements Doc needs to acknowledge these gaps, not paper over them.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What Project-Discovery Is Planning (High Level)\n\nWe're rebuilding our pipeline to take the same raw inputs (Zoom MP4s, Otter transcripts, artifact photos) and produce output comparable to the Golden Inputs. Push-button, repeatable.\n\n**Key things we learned that inform the rebuild:**\n\n- ~50% of sessions have no screenshots (transcript-only). The pipeline must handle this.\n- Business rule extraction is a first-class output, not a byproduct. Day 3 alone had 133.\n- Quality passes (cross-session, cross-day) catch things single-pass extraction misses: forward references, design evolutions, stakeholder threading, hidden confirmations.\n- The process gets richer as it goes -- each session benefits from everything extracted before it (growing corpus effect).\n- Cross-day enrichment is bidirectional: Day 3 findings enrich Day 1 entries, and vice versa.\n\n**We are not building yet.** We're reviewing the plan, identifying gaps (14 found so far), and incorporating operator feedback before any code changes.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The Two-Mode Vision\n\nThis isn't something to build for now. But it should inform how you evaluate your tooling during the audit.\n\n**Mode 1 -- During Discovery (day-by-day):**\n- Project-discovery processes each day's inputs that evening\n- Produces a \"slightly less golden\" day-level extraction (no full QP, no cross-day backward pass)\n- Hands that extraction to tap-discovery's pipeline\n- Tap-discovery produces intermediate outputs: Daily Brief, Facilitator's Guide, gap analysis\n- These outputs shape the next day's facilitation (what to probe deeper, what was missed, what needs clarification)\n- Repeat each night of the engagement\n\n**Mode 2 -- Post-Discovery (back at HQ):**\n- All days available. Project-discovery runs full extraction with cross-session QP, backward pass, enrichment detection\n- Produces Golden Inputs\n- Tap-discovery produces the Requirements Document from Golden Inputs\n\n**Why this matters for your audit:** Some of your existing tooling (Daily Briefs, Facilitator's Guides, gap analysis) may be exactly what Mode 1 needs. Don't throw it out just because the immediate mission is Mode 2 (Requirements Doc). Evaluate it against both modes.\n\n---\n\n## 7. What This Means for Your Audit\n\n1. **Lead with the Requirements Doc mission.** Evaluate every tool against: does this help me produce the Requirements Document from the Golden Inputs? If yes, keep it. If no, set it aside -- don't delete it.\n\n2. **Understand the gap between Golden Inputs and Requirements Doc.** The Golden Inputs give you extracted, cross-referenced, quality-checked discovery data. The Requirements Doc needs decomposed, prioritized, structured requirements. That gap is your pipeline's core job.\n\n3. **Don't rebuild what project-discovery will provide.** We're handling: raw input processing, session extraction, screen/artifact cataloging, business rule extraction, cross-session QP, cross-day enrichment. If your tooling duplicates this, note it as \"covered by upstream\" rather than \"needs rebuilding.\"\n\n4. **Do flag what you need from us that the Golden Inputs don't provide.** If the Requirements Doc process reveals that you need something structured differently, or additional data we didn't extract, or a different format -- that's valuable feedback for our rebuild.\n\n5. **Preserve Mode 1 tooling.** Anything that produces intermediate deliverables (briefs, guides, facilitation support) has a future even if it's not needed for the Requirements Doc. Tag it, don't trash it.\n\n6. **Stay client-agnostic, day-agnostic, project-agnostic.** This discovery was 3 days with TAP. The next might be 2 days remote with a different client. Neither project should hardcode engagement-specific assumptions.\n\n---\n\n## 8. What's Coming Next (After Both Golden Outputs Exist)\n\nOnce the Requirements Doc is delivered and project-discovery's pipeline rebuild plan is finalized:\n\n1. **Shared vision doc** -- How both projects fit together. What each side owns. Where the handoff happens. How Mode 1 and Mode 2 work end-to-end.\n2. **Boundary spec** -- Formal interface contract between project-discovery output and tap-discovery input. Format, structure, what's guaranteed, what's optional.\n3. **Coordinated rebuild** -- Both projects rebuild their pipelines with shared understanding. No overlap, no gaps, no cross-contamination.\n\nNone of this happens until the Requirements Doc ships. Focus on the deliverable.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Ground Rules for Cross-Project Work\n\nThese protect both projects from the kind of confusion that cost us 3 days when a PDF assumption propagated unchecked:\n\n- **No cross-writing.** Project-discovery does not write to tap-discovery's directories (except at explicit Phase 5 handoff). Tap-discovery does not write to project-discovery's directories.\n- **No shared assumptions without documentation.** If one project assumes something about the other's output format, behavior, or timeline, it goes in a shared doc -- not in a memory file, not in a brain doc, not in a conversation.\n- **Feedback flows through the operator.** If tap-discovery needs something different from project-discovery (or vice versa), that request goes through the operator, not directly between projects. This prevents context pollution.\n- **Each project owns its own context.** Brain docs, memory files, and CLAUDE.md stay within their project. Cross-project understanding lives in shared docs that both projects reference.\n"},"uuid":"4d3a38c4-53ba-4fd0-9d24-94076f12b333","timestamp":"2026-04-01T13:16:56.727Z","permissionMode":"acceptEdits"}

What the Golden Inputs Give You\n\nEach day's output follows the Output Architecture spec (with 14 agreed corrections):\n\n- **Screen Catalog** -- PART 1 (new screens) + PART 2 (cross-day enrichments). What the Golden Inputs Do NOT Give You\n\nThe Golden Inputs are extraction-level output. They document what was observed, discussed, captured, and cross-referenced. They are not:\n\n- **Decomposed into concepts/epics/stories** -- That's your pipeline's job. The raw material is there (screens, artifacts, business rules, stakeholder statements) but the decomposition into requirements hierarchy hasn't happened.\n- **Prioritized** -- Business rules are sourced and attributed but not ranked. Some are CEO mandates, some are operator preferences, some are system constraints. Your pipeline needs to assess priority.\n- **Resolved where stakeholders disagree** -- The Golden Inputs document contradictions and design evolutions (e.g., \"one DB with location IDs\" from Day 2 vs \"3 databases\" from Tim's SRD). They flag these, they don't resolve them. Resolution is a requirements-level decision.\n- **Structured for SRD vs PRD split** -- The Tim SRD extraction covers technical approach. The day-level catalogs cover functional needs. But the PRD/SRD boundary (what vs how) hasn't been drawn through the data. Your pipeline draws that line.\n- **Complete on their own** -- The Golden Inputs capture what happened in 3 days of discovery. There are known gaps: Reports submenu never opened, Management category unexplored, Gadsden facility not visited. The Requirements Doc needs to acknowledge these gaps, not paper over them.\n\n---\n\n## 5. What Project-Discovery Is Planning (High Level)\n\nWe're rebuilding our pipeline to take the same raw inputs (Zoom MP4s, Otter transcripts, artifact photos) and produce output comparable to the Golden Inputs. Push-button, repeatable.\n\n**Key things we learned that inform the rebuild:**\n\n- ~50% of sessions have no screenshots (transcript-only). The pipeline must handle this.\n- Business rule extraction is a first-class output, not a byproduct. Day 3 alone had 133.\n- Quality passes (cross-session, cross-day) catch things single-pass extraction misses: forward references, design evolutions, stakeholder threading, hidden confirmations.\n- The process gets richer as it goes -- each session benefits from everything extracted before it (growing corpus effect).\n- Cross-day enrichment is bidirectional: Day 3 findings enrich Day 1 entries, and vice versa.\n\n**We are not building yet.** We're reviewing the plan, identifying gaps (14 found so far), and incorporating operator feedback before any code changes.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The Two-Mode Vision\n\nThis isn't something to build for now. But it should inform how you evaluate your tooling during the audit.\n\n**Mode 1 -- During Discovery (day-by-day):**\n- Project-discovery processes each day's inputs that evening\n- Produces a \"slightly less golden\" day-level extraction (no full QP, no cross-day backward pass)\n- Hands that extraction to tap-discovery's pipeline\n- Tap-discovery produces intermediate outputs: Daily Brief, Facilitator's Guide, gap analysis\n- These outputs shape the next day's facilitation (what to probe deeper, what was missed, what needs clarification)\n- Repeat each night of the engagement\n\n**Mode 2 -- Post-Discovery (back at HQ):**\n- All days available. Project-discovery runs full extraction with cross-session QP, backward pass, enrichment detection\n- Produces Golden Inputs\n- Tap-discovery produces the Requirements Document from Golden Inputs\n\n**Why this matters for your audit:** Some of your existing tooling (Daily Briefs, Facilitator's Guides, gap analysis) may be exactly what Mode 1 needs. Don't throw it out just because the immediate mission is Mode 2 (Requirements Doc). Evaluate it against both modes.\n\n---\n\n## 7. What This Means for Your Audit\n\n1. **Lead with the Requirements Doc mission.** Evaluate every tool against: does this help me produce the Requirements Document from the Golden Inputs? If yes, keep it. If no, set it aside -- don't delete it.\n\n2. **Understand the gap between Golden Inputs and Requirements Doc.** The Golden Inputs give you extracted, cross-referenced, quality-checked discovery data. The Requirements Doc needs decomposed, prioritized, structured requirements. That gap is your pipeline's core job.\n\n3. **Don't rebuild what project-discovery will provide.** We're handling: raw input processing, session extraction, screen/artifact cataloging, business rule extraction, cross-session QP, cross-day enrichment. If your tooling duplicates this, note it as \"covered by upstream\" rather than \"needs rebuilding.\"\n\n4. **Do flag what you need from us that the Golden Inputs don't provide.** If the Requirements Doc process reveals that you need something structured differently, or additional data we didn't extract, or a different format -- that's valuable feedback for our rebuild.\n\n5. **Preserve Mode 1 tooling.** Anything that produces intermediate deliverables (briefs, guides, facilitation support) has a future even if it's not needed for the Requirements Doc. Tag it, don't trash it.\n\n6. **Stay client-agnostic, day-agnostic, project-agnostic.** This discovery was 3 days with TAP. The next might be 2 days remote with a different client. Neither project should hardcode engagement-specific assumptions.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Format, structure, what's guaranteed, what's optional.\n3. **Coordinated rebuild** -- Both projects rebuild their pipelines with shared understanding. Ground Rules for Cross-Project Work\n\nThese protect both projects from the kind of confusion that cost us 3 days when a PDF assumption propagated unchecked:\n\n- **No cross-writing.** Project-discovery does not write to tap-discovery's directories (except at explicit Phase 5 handoff). Tap-discovery does not write to project-discovery's directories.\n- **No shared assumptions without documentation.** If one project assumes something about the other's output format, behavior, or timeline, it goes in a shared doc -- not in a memory file, not in a brain doc, not in a conversation.\n- **Feedback flows through the operator.** If tap-discovery needs something different from project-discovery (or vice versa), that request goes through the operator, not directly between projects. This prevents context pollution.\n- **Each project owns its own context.** Brain docs, memory files, and CLAUDE.md stay within their project.
